alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature of Pope Gregory the Great, haloed and wearing a blue chasuble and white pallium with red crosses, seated frontally on a cushioned throne before an arched niche, from which a jewelled votive crown hangs above his head. A white dove perches at his shoulder by his ear. He holds a gold-bound book and touches an open book on a tall wooden lectern at right. At left, behind a large white curtain hung between columns, a tonsured notary in blue leans forward, piercing the curtain with his stylus and holding a wax tablet. A red-tiled roof and columns with foliate capitals close the scene within a red and gold border
caption: Saint Gregory the Great Inspired by the Holy Spirit, with His Notary. Detached leaf from the Registrum Gregorii, Trier, between 983 and 993. Paint and gold on parchment, c. 26.5 × 19.5 cm. Trier, Stadtbibliothek (Wissenschaftliche Bibliothek der Stadt Trier), Hs. 171/1626a.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature of a young, beardless emperor enthroned frontally beneath a canopy with a red tiled roof and arches on marbled columns. He holds a long sceptre and a golden orb marked with a cross, and wears a pink tunic under a red mantle sprinkled with gold. Two crowned and veiled women stand on each side offering golden spheres, against a pale sky and green ground within a narrow red and gold border
caption: Emperor Otto Enthroned, Receiving the Homage of Four Provinces. Detached leaf from the Registrum Gregorii, Trier, between 983 and 993. Paint and gold on parchment, 27 × 19.8 cm. Chantilly, Musée Condé, Ms. 14 bis.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on a painted purple ground. At the centre, inside a pointed gold mandorla, Christ sits on a cushioned throne, wearing a light blue tunic and a red mantle, with a cross-inscribed halo; he blesses with his right hand and holds a jewelled book in his left. In four green circles at the corners, haloed evangelists sit at lecterns writing on scrolls or in books. Four smaller roundels between them contain the evangelist symbols: an eagle above, a winged lion at left, a winged ox at right and an angel below. Gold Latin verses run across the purple ground, and an orange and gold border frames the page
caption: Christ in Majesty with the Four Evangelists and Their Symbols. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 1v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page. At left, a tall panel painted in deep purple holds a monumental gold initial B, its shafts edged with white interlace and its bowls filled with gold scrolling vines on grounds of blue, green and pink dotted with white. Gold capitals beside and below the letter complete the words BEATISSIMO PAPAE DAMASO HIERONIMUS, followed by a smaller gold initial N beginning NOVUM OPUS FACERE ME COGIS EX. At right, a single column of text in gold minuscule on bare parchment continues Jerome's letter. The folio number 3 appears at the top right.
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and Trier workshop, Initial B and Incipit of Jerome's Letter to Pope Damasus (Novum opus). Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Gold and paint on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 3r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature framed by an arch on two marbled columns with pink foliate capitals, set against a pink wall with blind arcades. In the lunette, a haloed, winged angel seen half-length against a blue ground holds an inscribed scroll. Below it a purple band carries two lines of gold capitals. Red curtains hang from the beam and are tied around the columns. Beneath them, on a green ground, the haloed, bearded evangelist Matthew sits on a folding stool with a red cushion, wearing a white tunic and a mauve mantle, a closed gold book on his lap and his bare feet on a footstool, writing in a book on a tall turned lectern with an inkhorn
caption: Saint Matthew Writing, with His Symbol, the Angel. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 15v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. A large gold monogram combining the letters L and I, filled with interlace in gold, blue and white and ending in knotted terminals, stands on a deep purple panel. Beside it, tall gold capitals spell BER and GENERATIO, and a gold line beneath reads NIS IHU XPI FILII DAVID. A green field surrounds the panel, enclosed by a broad gold frame with bands of scrolling vines. Square corner fields hold the evangelist symbols: an angel at top left, an eagle at top right, a lion at bottom left and an ox at bottom right. Circular medallions at the middle of each side contain busts of young, beardless men on gold grounds. The parchment is torn and holed in the green area at left
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and Trier workshop, Incipit Page of the Gospel of Matthew (Liber generationis), with Evangelist Symbols and Four Ruler Medallions. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Gold and paint on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 16v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature framed by a large arch on marbled green columns with gold spiral ornament. In the lunette, a haloed, winged golden lion holding a book lies on a purple band inscribed with two lines of gold capitals. Below, within a pink arcade of three arches on slender columns against an ochre ground, the haloed evangelist Mark, elderly and grey-haired, sits frontally on a throne with animal-head arms and lion-paw feet. He wears a blue chasuble and a white pallium marked with black crosses, holds a closed book, and dips a quill into an inkwell on a slender turned stand at left. At right stands a tall cabinet lectern with books and a hanging scroll. A faint sketch of a seated figure is visible in the lower margin
caption: Saint Mark Enthroned as Bishop, with His Symbol, the Lion. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 52v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature framed by an arch on marbled columns with white vine tendrils and pink foliate capitals. In the lunette, a haloed, winged, horned ox in reddish brown reclines on a purple band inscribed with two lines of gold capitals, its forelegs on a closed book. Below, between drawn mauve curtains and slender white columns on a green ground, the haloed evangelist Luke, with white hair and beard, sits on a gold block throne. He wears a light blue tunic and an orange-red mantle with a circular fold over his belly, holds a pen in one hand, and reaches with the other to an open book on a grey pedestal lectern. Behind him at left, a tall stand holds a book showing the opening lines of his Gospel. His bare feet rest on an arcaded footstool
caption: Saint Luke Writing, with His Symbol, the Ox. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 75v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature framed by an arch on pink marbled columns with blue foliate capitals; gold vine scrolls fill the mauve spandrels and bands of blue and green leaf ornament run around the arch. In the pink lunette, a haloed golden eagle with raised wings grips a closed book in its talon above a purple band inscribed in gold capitals. Below, against a blue ground, the young, beardless, haloed evangelist John sits on a large jewelled gold throne draped with a green cloth. He wears a blue tunic and a rose mantle, holds closed white books on his lap, raises his left hand with open palm, and looks upward toward the eagle. At right stands a tall arcaded pedestal lectern with a sloping desk bearing an inkwell and quill. A white inscription above reads IOHANNES APOSTOLUS ET EVANGELISTA.
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii, Saint John the Evangelist Inspired, with His Symbol, the Eagle. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 115v.

alt: Page of a Carolingian Gospel book on pale parchment. Across the top margin runs a single line in small reddish-brown medieval minuscule: the ownership note of Saint Martin's church on the Moselle with a curse against theft.
caption: Ownership note of the church of Saint Martin, Trier, and text of Jerome’s letter to Pope Damasus (Novum opus). Strahov Gospels, text written in uncial script, probably at Tours, c. 860; ownership note in a later minuscule hand. Ink on parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 2r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on purple-stained parchment. In a narrow upper register on a lilac ground, a half-length haloed angel with blue-grey wings holds a gold book, flanked by faded gold inscriptions. Below, a purple band carries a line of gold capitals beginning HOC EVANGELIUM. In the main field, on a green ground with areas of paint loss, the haloed evangelist Matthew, young and beardless, sits bent forward on a gold block throne with a red cushion. He wears a white tunic and a deep purple mantle and writes on a long sheet laid across a desk on a red turned stand. His bare feet rest on a blue-green footstool. Gold capitals beside his head name him. A small parchment tab with Gothic script projects from the left edge
caption: Saint Matthew Writing, with His Symbol, the Angel. Leaf added to the Strahov Gospels (text written at Tours, c. 860), Trier, church of Saint Martin, late tenth century. Paint and gold on purple-stained parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 8v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on purple-stained parchment. In an upper register on a pale pink ground, a haloed, winged golden lion with raised tail rests a forepaw on a closed book. Below it, a purple band carries one line of gold capitals: MARCUM TERRIBILIS DESIGNAT FORMA LEONIS. In the main field, on a warm golden-orange ground, the haloed, tonsured evangelist Mark sits on a violet block throne with a green cushion. He wears a light blue tunic and a rose mantle with a circular fold over his thigh, and dips a quill into an inkwell on a tall foliate stand at left, while a long inscribed scroll in his other hand unrolls toward a lectern on a green column at right. His bare feet rest on a grey footstool. A small parchment tab projects from the left edge
caption: Saint Mark Writing, with His Symbol, the Lion. Leaf added to the Strahov Gospels (text written at Tours, c. 860), Trier, church of Saint Martin, late tenth century. Paint and gold on purple-stained parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 69v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on purple-stained parchment. In an upper register on a blue ground, a haloed, winged, horned ox in reddish brown reclines over a book. Below it, a purple band carries one line of gold capitals beginning LUCAS AETHEREI SPECIEM. In the main field, on a rose ground, the haloed evangelist Luke, young and beardless, sits on a gold folding stool with animal-head terminals and a red cushion, wrapped in a green mantle over a blue tunic. He rests his chin on one hand and holds a small scroll in the other, gazing at an open book on a tall mauve pedestal lectern from which a scroll hangs. His bare feet rest on a gold footstool. A small parchment tab projects from the left edge
caption: Saint Luke in Contemplation, with His Symbol, the Ox. Leaf added to the Strahov Gospels (text written at Tours, c. 860), Trier, church of Saint Martin, late tenth century. Paint and gold on purple-stained parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 107v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on purple-stained parchment. In an upper register on a pale mauve ground, a haloed eagle with spread wings and head in profile perches above a book. Below it, a purple band carries one line of gold capitals: EST AQUILA ALTA PETENS NARRANS DIVINA IOHANNES. In the main field, on a blue-violet ground, the haloed evangelist John, elderly with long hair and a grey beard, sits frontally on a gold block throne with a green cushion. He wears a white tunic and a bright red mantle and holds an open book filled with script in one hand, writing in it with a quill held in the other. His feet rest on a green footstool. At right stands a tall mauve pedestal lectern with an arched niche, bearing scrolls and an inkwell. A small parchment tab projects from the left edge.
caption: Saint John the Evangelist Writing, with His Symbol, the Eagle. Leaf added to the Strahov Gospels (text written at Tours, c. 860), Trier, church of Saint Martin, late tenth century. Paint and gold on purple-stained parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 176v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature within an orange and gold frame. Christ hangs on a gold cross against a lilac sky above and a deep blue ground below, his arms straight, his bearded head with a cross-inscribed halo inclined to one side, his pale body modelled with a rounded abdomen and an orange loincloth knotted at the waist. Above the crossbar, two roundels show the Sun as a young man with a radiant halo and the Moon as a veiled woman beneath a crescent. Gold letters near the top of the cross name Jesus Christ our Lord. At left the Virgin Mary, veiled in white and purple over a blue gown, bows her head in grief; at right the young Saint John, in a pink tunic and green mantle, holds a jewelled book and raises his hand. Gold inscriptions name both. They stand on a green ground with small plants.
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii (attributed), The Crucifixion with the Virgin Mary and Saint John, the Sun and the Moon. Lorsch Sacramentary, Trier, c. 975–980, for the abbey of Lorsch. Paint and gold on parchment. Chantilly, Bibliothèque du château (Musée Condé), Ms. 40 (formerly 1447), fol. 4v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on pale parchment dominated by a monumental gold initial T. Its upright stem is filled with a narrow band of silver-white interlace, interrupted at mid-height. From the stem, symmetrical gold acanthus scrolls spiral outward on both sides, forming four roundels with rosettes at their centres: the upper two on violet grounds, the lower two on turquoise grounds, all outlined in orange. To the right of the stem's foot stands a gold capital E, and beneath it the word IGITUR in large gold capitals completes the opening words Te igitur. Faint letters from the other side of the leaf show through the parchment
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and Trier workshop (attributed), Initial T Opening the Canon of the Mass (Te igitur). Lorsch Sacramentary, Trier, c. 975–980, for the abbey of Lorsch. Gold and paint on parchment. Chantilly, Bibliothèque du château (Musée Condé), Ms. 40 (formerly 1447), fol. 5r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on pale parchment with a rectangular decorated panel. A gold initial B dominates a deep purple field: its tall shaft curls up into a knotted loop that breaks through the top of the frame, and its large round bowl, joined to the shaft by gold interlace knots, holds a green ground filled with a gold beast whose head with pointed ears and open jaws emerges from a dense knot of interlace ending in leaves. Smaller gold and coloured letters E and A stand above the bowl and T, I and S beside its base; below, gold capitals read SIMO PAPAE DA / MASO HERONIMUS. Small white and gold sprays are scattered over the purple. The panel is framed by gold bands, a lilac border with gold vine scrolls, a dark green border with gold foliage, orange corner squares with gold rosettes, and leaf-shaped finials at the outer corners
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Initial B and Incipit of Jerome's Letter to Pope Damasus (Novum opus). Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 1v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. On a mauve panel, a gold monogram combines the letters L and I: the L runs down the left side and along the bottom, the I rises in the centre, both filled with white interlace, ending in gold knots. Symmetrical gold scrolls spring from the I, forming four roundels with rosettes on blue grounds over green. Small gold letters spell BER, GENE, and at the bottom RATIONIS. The panel is enclosed by gold, pink, lilac and orange borders with stylised plant stems, blue corner squares with foliage, and gold foliate crests. Four blue squares at the midpoints of the frame hold gold medallions with busts of a young beardless man, each surrounded by a tiny inscription. Gold rosette finials project from the outer corners
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Incipit of the Gospel of Matthew (Liber generationis), with Four Medallions of the Emperor Otto. Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 16r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. On a deep purple panel, a monumental gold initial I rises through the centre, its stem left partly in bare parchment and bound by gold bands, with dense knots of gold interlace at top and bottom that break through the frame. Symmetrical gold scrolls spring from the stem, enclosing a green oval at the centre and four roundels with gold rosettes on lilac grounds. Gold capitals NI and TI stand in the upper corners and V and M in the lower corners, spelling INITIUM. The frame consists of orange, gold and green bands with gold interlace, with lilac acanthus leaves at the corners, gold interlace knots at the midpoints of the sides, and heart-shaped gold finials projecting diagonally from the outer corners. A short note in small minuscule appears in the right margin
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Incipit of the Gospel of Mark (Initium). Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 65r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. On a deep purple panel with stepped lilac edges, a monumental gold initial Q fills the upper part: its oval bowl encloses a green field with symmetrical gold vine scrolls, gold rosettes and small white quatrefoils on lilac grounds, and its tail descends as a straight vertical stem filled with a white scroll pattern. Beside the stem, gold capitals read UONI AM / QUI DEM, completing QUONIAM QUIDEM, with small white sprigs scattered on the purple. The frame consists of orange, gold and white bands with gold interlace. Bevelled square fields at the midpoints of the sides hold geometric motifs: a saltire pattern at top and bottom, eight-pointed stars at left and right. Heart-shaped gold finials project diagonally from the outer corners
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Incipit of the Gospel of Luke (Quoniam quidem). Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 98r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. On a deep purple panel, a gold monogram combines the letters I and N: the I rises through the centre, filled with white interlace, while the N is formed by two uprights of dense gold interlace and foliage joined by a diagonal band of white interlace. Gold capitals read PRINCIPIO above and ERAT VERBU(M) below. A small square at the centre of the monogram shows a white Lamb of God with a slender staff. Four further squares on the axes of the frame hold the evangelist symbols on gold grounds: the eagle above, the winged ox at left, the winged lion at right and the angel below. The frame has gold, green and blue bands with white foliate ornament, gold foliate crests at the midpoints and gold fleur-de-lis finials at the corners. A short note in small minuscule appears in the right margin
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Incipit of the Gospel of John (In principio erat Verbum), with the Lamb of God and the Four Evangelist Symbols. Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 154r.

alt: Twelfth-century Pisan painted cross on a gold ground. A living, frontal Christ with open eyes, a relief halo and a long knotted loincloth stands with horizontal arms against a dark blue cross. The crossbar terminals show the Last Supper and the Washing of the Feet. Six Passion and post-Resurrection scenes, including the Mocking, the Crucifixion, the Holy Women at the Tomb and the Supper at Emmaus, flank his body. The damaged cimasa shows an Ascension and the foot shows Pentecost
caption: Painted Cross with Christus Triumphans and Gospel Scenes (Croce n. 15), Pisa, second half of the 12th century. Tempera and gold on panel, 282 × 236 cm. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1578; from the church of the Santo Sepolcro, Pisa.
entry: Maestro della Croce del Santo Sepolcro

alt: Romanesque painted cross showing a living Christ with open eyes and a gold nimbus, arms stretched horizontally, wearing a long translucent blue-grey loincloth. Six small Passion and post-Resurrection scenes flank his torso, a Pentecost fills the top panel, and a standing prophet appears at each end of the crossbar. Two superimposed Latin inscriptions are visible above his head.
caption: Master of the San Frediano Cross (first painting) and Master of Rosano (attr., repainting), Painted Cross with Christ Triumphant, Scenes of the Passion and Resurrection, Pentecost, and the Prophets David and Isaiah. First painting c. 1110–1120; repainted c. 1130–1140. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, church of San Frediano. The face of Christ belongs to the earlier layer; the narrative scenes, cimasa and terminals belong to the twelfth-century repainting uncovered in the restoration of 1960–1972.
entry: Maestro della Croce di San Frediano

alt: Twelfth-century painted cross from the monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano: a living, open-eyed Christ in a blue loincloth stands against a gold ground, arms outstretched along a blue crossbar, flanked by six small Passion and Resurrection scenes in two columns, with mourning figures in the arm terminals and the Denial of Peter on the lower shaft, the whole cross displayed on a moulded stone corbel against a black background
caption: Painted Cross with Passion Scenes, c. 1129–1134, tempera and gold on chestnut panel, 253 × 230 cm (Fondazione Zeri). Rignano sull'Arno (Florence), monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano.

alt: Romanesque church of San Pietro in Villore at San Giovanni d'Asso: stone lower façade with blind arcades and carved portal, brick upper storey with oculus, bell-gable and cypresses
caption: San Pietro in Villore, San Giovanni d'Asso (Montalcino, Siena), second half of the 12th century. Three-quarter view of the façade: lower register in squared sandstone and alberese with four blind arches on half-columns flanking the splayed portal; upper register in brick, rebuilt after later damage, with oculus; the brick bell-gable dates from the early 20th-century restoration.

entry: Maestro di San Pietro in Villore

alt: Painted cross with a living Christ on a deep blue ground, open-eyed beneath a raised gilded halo, his arms outstretched along the crossbar. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark blue mantle on the left and Saint John in a red mantle on the right. The terminals of the arms hold the four Evangelist symbols. The top shows the Virgin between two angels and the foot shows small scenes of the Denial of Peter
caption: Christus Triumphans (Cross of Santa Maria degli Angeli), c. 1210–1220. Tempera and gold on shaped panel, 174.7 × 140.5 cm. Lucca, Museo Nazionale di Villa Guinigi, inv. 226; from the monastery of Santa Maria degli Angeli, Lucca. Signed: BERLINGERIUS ME PINXIT.

alt: Painted cross with a slender, living Christ on a dark ground framed by red bands. His head, under a raised gilded halo, tilts towards his right shoulder with a sorrowful expression, and a thin white loincloth is knotted at the centre. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark blue mantle and Saint John in a red mantle, each raising a hand to the cheek in grief. The red top panel bears the monogram IC XC, and the ends of the crossbar have been cut away
caption: Crucifix from the abbey of San Salvatore at Fucecchio, c. 1230–1235. Tempera and gold on shaped panel, c. 156 × 100 cm (arm terminals detached). Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 5773. Signed: BERLINGERIUS VULTERRANUS ME PINXIT (recovered during the 1981 restoration).

alt: Arched gold-ground panel within a raised red frame. The Virgin, in a dark purple mantle marked with gold stars, holds the Christ Child on her right arm and raises her other hand towards him. The Child wears a pale blue tunic and a gold-hatched mantle, holds an open book inscribed in Greek, and looks up at his mother. Both figures wear applied metal crowns
caption: Berlinghiero (Berlinghiero di Melanese), attributed, Madonna and Child, known as the Madonna di sotto gli organi, c. 1220 (before 1226?). Tempera and gold on arched panel, 93 × 55 cm. Pisa, Cathedral, altar of the Madonna di sotto gli organi. Extensively restored in 1789–1790; the crowns are copies made in 1912.

alt: Gold-ground panel with the half-length Virgin in a deep blue mantle edged in orange and marked with gold stars. Her long, narrow face with almond eyes looks out sideways with a melancholy expression. She points with long fingers of her right hand towards the Christ Child, who sits on her left arm in an orange robe hatched with gold, holding a red scroll and raising his right hand in blessing. Red Greek monograms flank the Virgin's head
caption: Madonna and Child, possibly 1230s. Tempera on wood, gold ground; overall 80.3 × 53.7 cm, painted surface 76.2 × 49.5 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Irma N. Straus, 1960 (60.173).

alt: Small open triptych on gold ground. In the centre the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, holds the Christ Child, who embraces her with his cheek pressed to hers, while two angels fly in the upper corners. The left wing shows the Crucifixion of Saint Andrew above Saints Francis and Paul; the right wing shows Christ in a mandorla with the instruments of the Passion above the deacon saints Stephen and Lawrence
caption: Virgin and Child with Saints, triptych (tabernacle), c. 1230s. Tempera and gold on poplar panel; overall 42.6 × 51.5 cm (centre 42.8 × 27 cm; left wing 42.5 × 12.5 cm; right wing 42.4 × 12 cm). Cleveland, The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust, 1966.237.

alt: Arched gold-ground panel in a plain gilded frame. The Virgin, in a dark blue-green mantle with gold stars on her forehead and shoulder and a fringed, striped border, holds the Christ Child on her left arm. The Child, in an orange-red robe, raises his right hand in blessing and holds a small white scroll, while her long-fingered hand rests beneath him. The upper corners retain only worn fragments of painted figures
caption: Workshop of Berlinghiero di Melanese, Central panel of a triptych: Virgin and Child “Hodegetria”; (in the spandrels above) The Annunciation, c. 1225–1250. Tempera and gold leaf on panel, 71.8 × 48.9 cm; frame 84.8 × 59.7 cm. Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, Gift of Wachovia Bank and Trust Company, GL.57.16.1.

alt: Painted cross with a living Christ on a dark blue ground edged with red pearled bands. His head, under a gilded halo, inclines to one side, and he wears a long pink loincloth. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark mantle and Saint John in a pink mantle, above small scenes of the Capture of Christ and the Holy Women at the Tomb. At the top Christ blesses between two angels, small winged Evangelist symbols occupy the ends of the arms, and small figures flank the feet
caption: Berlinghieri workshop (attributed to Berlinghiero and his circle, or to Bonaventura Berlinghieri), Painted Cross (Tereglio Cross), c. 1235–1245. Tempera and gold on panel. Tereglio (Coreglia Antelminelli, Lucca), church of Santa Maria Assunta; probably from the church of San Martino at Bori (Alborio). Restored 1998.

alt: Gabled gold-ground panel showing a tall, frontal Saint Francis in a dark hooded habit, blessing and holding a book, with stigmata on his hands and feet and a half-length winged angel on each side of his head. Three small narrative scenes run down each side: at upper left the Stigmatization, at upper right Francis beneath a canopy with kneeling laymen; a dated inscription lies between his feet
caption: Saint Francis and Six Stories (three from his life, three posthumous miracles), 1235. Tempera and gold on panel, c. 160 × 123 cm (151 × 114 cm according to the diocese of Pescia). Pescia, Church of San Francesco.

alt: Gold-ground panel dominated by a dark blue cross on which the dead Christ hangs with bowed head, flanked by two angels. Groups of mourners stand in the upper corners; below are the Way to Calvary at left and the Deposition at right, all within a dark ornamented border
caption: Attributed to Bonaventura Berlinghieri (or Master of the Oblate Cross), Crucifixion with Mourners, the Way to Calvary and the Deposition, right wing of a diptych from Santa Chiara, Lucca, c. 1255–1257. Tempera and gold on panel, 103 × 61 cm. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 n. 8575–8576.

alt: Two hinged gold-ground panels side by side. On the left, the Virgin in a deep blue mantle holds the Christ Child cheek to cheek, surrounded by small standing saints, among them two Franciscan friars and the Archangel Michael. On the right, the dead Christ hangs from a blue cross between mourners, above scenes of the Way to Calvary and the Deposition
caption: Attributed to Bonaventura Berlinghieri (or Master of the Oblate Cross), Diptych with the Virgin and Child with Saints and the Crucifixion with Scenes of the Passion, from Santa Chiara, Lucca, c. 1255–1257. Tempera and gold on panel, 103 × 123 cm overall (each wing 103 × 61 cm). Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 nos. 8575–8576.

alt: Painted cross with a living, open-eyed Christ in a pink loincloth on a dark ground edged with red, his arms outstretched along the crossbar. The Virgin and Saint John stand full-length in the gold side fields above two small scenes. At the top, a blessing Christ between two angels sits above a red titulus; small figures fill the ends of the crossbar
caption: Circle of Bonaventura Berlinghieri, Crucifix (Triumphant Christ), 1250-60, tempera and gold leaf on wood panel, 286 x 187 x 6 cm, Palazzo Barberini, Roma.

alt: Irregular, worm-eaten fragment of a painted cross showing the head and upper chest of a living Christ. His eyes are open, his long dark hair falls in wavy strands onto his shoulders, and his bearded face is set within a raised gilded halo with empty round sockets for inlays. A strip of blue cross ground survives at the right, and the edges are broken bare wood and gesso
caption: School of Bonaventura Berlinghieri (Lucca), Crucifix (fragment: head and chest of Christ), c. 1245–1255. Tempera and gold on panel, 43 × 34 cm. Avignon, Musée du Petit Palais, inv. Calvet 22812.

alt: Damaged fragment of the end of a painted cross. A long horizontal arm of Christ, modelled in greenish-yellow flesh, lies against a dark blue ground framed by red bands with rows of small circles. The open hand is pierced by a nail wound from which three streams of blood fall. To the right, in the square terminal, a young winged figure with curly hair and a halo, in a red mantle over a blue-green tunic, holds a thin staff and inclines his head sorrowfully
caption: Lucchese or Pisan painter (attributed to Bonaventura Berlinghieri; also given to the Master of Calci), Fragment of a painted cross: left arm of Christ and terminal with a mourning figure (an angel, or Saint John in the Petit Palais notice), mid-13th century. Tempera and gold on panel. Rio de Janeiro, Museu Nacional de Belas Artes.
