alt: Fragmentary panel painting showing the Virgin in half length against bare, worm-eaten wood where the ground has been lost. She wears a deep blue maphorion with a gold border over a red dress, her large dark eyes gazing frontally; a child’s small right arm is raised in a caress against her cheek, his left arm reaches down toward her hands in the abraded lower zone, and a fragment of red drapery with a gold hem survives at her left shoulder where the lost Christ Child once sat. The lower zone, with the Virgin’s hands, is heavily abraded
caption: Giotto di Bondone (attributed), Madonna and Child (fragment), c. 1290. Tempera on panel, 81.5 × 41 cm. Borgo San Lorenzo (Mugello), Pieve di San Lorenzo. From the oratory of Sant’Omobono.

alt: Panel painting on gold ground showing the Virgin in half length, wearing a black mantle with broad gold-embroidered borders and fringes over a red dress, a jewelled band across her brow beneath the veil and a gold star on her shoulder. She supports the Christ Child on her left arm and raises her right hand, open, toward him. The Child, in a coral-red mantle over a pale gold-striped tunic, blesses with his right hand and holds a white scroll; both haloes are incised with dense vine ornament in the gold.
caption: Giotto di Bondone (attributed), Madonna and Child, c. 1297. Tempera and gold on panel. Private collection.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the young Francis, haloed and in a dark blue civilian mantle, walking through the main square of Assisi as a man kneels to spread his cloak on the ground before him. Behind rises the Roman temple of Minerva with six columns and a pediment containing a rose window, flanked by the civic tower at the left and a loggia-crowned building at the right. Two pairs of onlookers converse at the edges; a dark loss from a fallen lamp scars the blue sky.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop (this scene assigned by most of the critics to the Master of Saint Cecilia), The Homage of a Simple Man in the Piazza of Assisi, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene I, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the young haloed Francis, in a blue-grey tunic, handing his golden mantle to a poor knight in a red robe who grasps it with both hands. Francis's grey horse stands at the left with a red saddle cloth, lowering its head to graze. Behind, two rocky hills descend in a V toward the saint: a walled city with towers and a gate crowns the left summit, a church with a campanile the right
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Saint Francis Giving His Mantle to a Poor Knight, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene II, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the young Francis asleep, haloed, in a canopied bed whose wooden frame is drawn in perspective; Christ, with a cross-inscribed halo, leans over the sleeper and points with his raised arm toward a tall fantastic palace at the right. The palace rises in storeys of Gothic triple arches hung with shields and banners, above a two-storey classical loggia; the sky behind has lost its blue
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Dream of the Palace Full of Arms, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene III, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the young haloed Francis kneeling in prayer inside the ruined church of San Damiano, shown in section: the roof is broken open to bare rafters, the walls are cracked, and the apse with its green dome shelters a large painted crucifix of Duecento type standing on the altar. A marble parapet with Cosmatesque panels closes the church at the left.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Saint Francis Praying before the Crucifix of San Damiano, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene IV, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the young Francis, half-naked and haloed, raising his hands toward the hand of God that emerges from the sky at the top of the scene, while the Bishop of Assisi wraps his mantle around him at the right, flanked by clerics. At the left his father, in a yellow robe with the renounced clothes over his arm, is restrained by a citizen; behind him press the townspeople, with two children at the lower corner. Two buildings frame the empty centre: a palazzo with an external staircase at the left, the bishop’s residence with a classical loggia at the right
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Saint Francis Renouncing His Worldly Goods, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene V, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing Pope Innocent III asleep in a canopied bed hung with a patterned golden curtain, wearing his mitre, while two attendants sit drowsing at the bedside. At the left the Lateran basilica, with its portico and tall campanile, tilts perilously toward collapse, and the haloed Saint Francis, in the brown habit of his order, braces it upright on his shoulder; small statues crown the rooftops and the campanile.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Dream of Innocent III, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene VI, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing Pope Innocent III standing at the right, in a red cope and white mitre, handing the scroll of the Rule to the kneeling, haloed Saint Francis, who receives it with covered and open hands at the head of eleven kneeling, tonsured companions. Mitred prelates stand behind the pope and a mitred prelate in a gold-patterned cope sits at the right. The audience hall is hung with a richly patterned curtain beneath an arcaded gallery on carved corbels, under a blue ceiling
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Innocent III Approving the Rule of Saint Francis, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene VII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing Saint Francis in prayer, in profile against a great radiating aureole, borne through the night sky on a red chariot drawn by a rearing red horse. Below, a hut shown in section shelters a group of friars, some asleep and some waking in wonder, while at the right three friars stand outside, one flinging up his arm toward the apparition. A pale building complex rises at the upper left against the deep blue sky
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Vision of the Flaming Chariot, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene VIII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing five empty golden thrones draped with cloths of honour floating against a deep blue sky, the central one taller and set on a stepped pedestal. Below, an angel in red and green descends pointing toward Saint Francis, who kneels in prayer before the altar of a small church rendered in section, a lamp hanging on chains above the altar cross; at the lower left a companion friar looks up with raised hands, witnessing the vision
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Vision of the Thrones in Heaven, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene IX, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing a tall Gothic church with a campanile at the left, before which Saint Francis kneels in prayer while the friar Silvester stands and raises his arm toward the walled city of Arezzo at the right. Above the city’s packed towers and houses seven dark, bat-winged demons flees into the sky. Two citizens appear in the arched gates of the rusticated city wall.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Expulsion of the Demons from Arezzo, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene X, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the Sultan of Egypt enthroned at the right under a gabled Gothic canopy, pointing across the scene toward two or three Saracen priests who withdraw at the left, glancing back; a fire blazes on the ground between them. At the centre the haloed Saint Francis, with a companion friar behind him, stands beside the flames, hand on his breast, ready to enter them. Soldiers of the court stand behind the throne; above, a columned loggia with a coffered vault and its piers crowned by small gilded statues of winged figures.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Saint Francis before the Sultan (The Trial by Fire), Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XI, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing Saint Francis lifted into the night sky on a luminous white cloud, arms raised wide, face turned upward toward Christ, who leans down in half-length from a dark opening of heaven at the upper right, extending his hand in blessing. At the lower left four friars react with wonder before a fortified building with towers and an arched gate; at the right, trees rise on a rocky slope
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Ecstasy of Saint Francis, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the first Christmas crib, seen from inside the choir of a church: Saint Francis, haloed and in a deacon’s vestment, kneels to lay the haloed Christ Child in a manger beside an ox and an ass, while a priest celebrates at the altar under a gabled ciborium and friars sing open-mouthed around a lectern. Behind rises the back of the choir screen, with a pulpit upon it and a great painted crucifix seen from the reverse, tilted forward on its wooden support; women look in through the screen’s doorway and townspeople crowd at the left.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Institution of the Crib at Greccio, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XIII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi, in vertical format, showing a steep rocky mountainside with pale, silvery trees against a dark sky. At the centre Saint Francis kneels in profile on the slope, praying toward the rock above, his halo radiating fine lines of light. At the lower left two friars stand beside a saddled ass; at the lower right a peasant in a grey tunic and cap stretches full-length on the ground, propping himself on his hands to drink from the spring that has broken from the rock
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Miracle of the Spring, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XIV, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 200 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, entrance wall, left of the portal.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi, in vertical format, showing Saint Francis bending deeply toward a flock of birds gathered on the ground beneath a tall leafy tree, his hands lowered toward them in speech and blessing. Behind him a companion friar watches with a gesture of astonishment. The birds — doves, crows and jackdaws — stand in rows facing the saint, while others fly down the hillside to join them; pale silvery trees stand against a whitened sky over a dark slope
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Saint Francis Preaching to the Birds, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XV, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 200 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, entrance wall, right of the portal.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing a banquet interrupted by death. At the left, under a coffered canopy with a colonnaded loggia above, a table laid with a white cloth carries bread, a fish on a platter, knives and glasses; a companion friar sits at its end and Saint Francis stands behind it, haloed, his hand opened toward the right, where the knight of Celano lies collapsed in red robes amid his kneeling family. Behind them stand mourning women in white veils and young women with loose hair, and a man in red lifts his hands in grief
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Death of the Knight of Celano, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XVI, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing Saint Francis preaching in a Gothic vaulted hall of three bays, with blue rib vaults, trefoil arcading and a patterned hanging along the walls. The saint stands at the left, haloed, gesturing as he speaks; a friar sits on the floor below him. At the centre Pope Honorius III, in a red mantle and tiara, listens with his head leaning on his hand, surrounded by six cardinals seated to either side, variously attentive and conversing
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Saint Francis Preaching before Honorius III, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XVII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the chapter house of Arles in section: a Gothic hall with pointed arches, pierced quatrefoil roundels and columned windows opening onto night, under a blue lean-to ceiling. Saint Anthony of Padua, haloed, preaches standing at the left; in the central doorway Saint Francis appears with arms extended in the form of a cross, visible above the crowd of hooded friars who sit on benches and on the floor, most with their backs to him, only a few turning or lifting their eyes
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Apparition of Saint Francis at the Chapter of Arles, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XVIII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing Saint Francis kneeling on the rocky slope of La Verna, body turned to the right and face lifted, his hands raised and opened toward the crucified Christ who appears in the sky at the upper right, borne on six red seraph wings within a radiance; fine golden rays run from Christ’s wounds to the saint’s hands, feet and side. At the left stands a small pink chapel with its door open onto an altar; at the right a golden aedicula with a rose window shelters a seated friar absorbed in reading a book. Trees crown the faceted mountain.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Saint Francis Receiving the Stigmata on La Verna, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XIX, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi in three registers. Below, Saint Francis lies dead on a bier in his habit, surrounded by kneeling friars who kiss his stigmatized hands and press close in grief. In the middle zone stand rows of friars and clergy in white, with processional crosses and candles, one deacon in a crossed stole; a friar at the centre lifts his gaze upward. Above, the saint’s soul — a half-length Francis in a round glory — is carried to heaven by angels over a small white cloud against the blue
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Death of Saint Francis and the Ascension of His Soul, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XX, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing two deathbed visions side by side. At the left, within a golden loggia-like infirmary with arches, an external staircase, a tower and small statues on its gable, the dying friar Agostino sits up suddenly in bed, arms raised, supported and watched by astonished friars. At the right, in a chamber hung with a white swagged pall over a diapered curtain, the mitred Bishop of Assisi lies asleep in bed. A long branching crack runs through the right half of the scene
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Apparition of Saint Francis to Fra Agostino and to Bishop Guido of Assisi, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XXI, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the dead Saint Francis on his bier inside a church, before a screen beam from which hang lamps and three images: a gabled panel of the Virgin and Child enthroned, a great painted crucifix of Duecento type tilted forward on its support, and a panel of an archangel. Around the bier crowd friars with tall candles, clergy in white with books, and laymen in caps; at the centre the knight Jerome kneels over the body, his hand at the saint’s side wound
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Knight Jerome Verifying the Stigmata, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XXII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the funeral procession of Saint Francis halted before an ornate white church front with rose windows, sculpted gables and a statue-filled portal. The saint’s body lies on a bier draped with a gold-patterned pall; Saint Clare, haloed in her dark veil, bends over him and embraces him, while another nun lifts his hand and the Poor Clares crowd from the doorway and the right, grieving. At the left presses the lay cortège with tall candles; behind, a man in white climbs a tree, and a bird perches on the topmost gable.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Saint Clare and Her Companions Mourning Saint Francis at San Damiano, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XXIII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Heavily worn fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the canonization ceremony: a tall wooden tribune with a canopy and a gold-patterned hanging rises at the left, its occupants almost effaced; below stands an altar draped in white. Around it crowds the assembly — friars, citizens in caps, two mitred bishops at the right, and in the foreground kneeling veiled women. The upper zone and the papal figure are largely lost to abrasion
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Gregory IX Proclaiming the Canonization of Saint Francis, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XXIV, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Monumental painted cross by Giotto. The dead Christ hangs heavily with bowed head, sagging body and overlapping feet against a red apron patterned in gold; half-length figures of the mourning Virgin and Saint John occupy the lateral terminals, a trilingual titulus the summit, and the rock of Golgotha with the skull of Adam the trapezoidal foot
caption: Crucifix, c. 1290–1295, tempera and gold on panel, 578 × 406 cm. Florence, Basilica di Santa Maria Novella.

alt: Panel painting by Giotto on gold ground showing the Virgin enthroned frontally, in a blue-black mantle over a red dress, holding the Christ Child on her left knee; the Child, in a pale blue tunic and pink mantle, raises his right hand in blessing and holds a scroll. Behind the throne’s patterned cloth of honour two angels lean inward over the backrest, hands resting on it. The throne bears cosmatesque inlay and a red cushion, and a pink finial crowns the gold ground; the panel’s edges are cut, with the modern support visible around the painted field
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Angels, c. 1295. Tempera and gold on panel, 180 × 90 cm (cut down on all sides). Florence, Museo Diocesano di Santo Stefano al Ponte; from the church of San Giorgio alla Costa.

alt: Five-panel gabled polyptych by Giotto on gold ground: at the centre the half-length Virgin holds the Christ Child, who reaches toward her; to the left Saint Nicholas in bishop's vestments and Saint John the Evangelist with book and pen, to the right a saint in a pallium with a staff and a book, and Saint Benedict in a dark habit; a small bust in a medallion crowns each pointed gable.
caption: Madonna and Child with Saints Nicholas, John the Evangelist, Peter and Benedict (Badia Polyptych), c. 1295–1300, tempera and gold on panel, 142 × 337 cm. Florence, Galleria degli Uffizi, from the Badia Fiorentina.

alt: Painted cross by Giotto in Rimini: the dead Christ hangs with bowed head and nearly vertical body against a dark field edged in gold, over an apron of gold damask patterning; a white translucent loincloth wraps the hips, a red tablet at the summit bears the Latin titulus, and the lateral terminals are lost
caption: Crucifix, c. 1300, tempera and gold on panel, 430 × 303 cm. Rimini, Tempio Malatestiano (Cathedral Basilica of Santa Colomba), from the church of San Francesco.

alt: Gabled panel by Giotto: the Virgin enthroned in a Gothic marble tabernacle holds the blessing Christ Child; two angels kneel in the foreground offering vases of lilies and roses, two more hold crowns beside the throne, and ranks of angels and saints gather in depth on either side against a gold ground
caption: Virgin and Child Enthroned with Angels and Saints (Ognissanti Madonna), c. 1305–1310, tempera and gold on panel, 325 × 204 cm. Florence, Galleria degli Uffizi, from the church of Ognissanti.

alt: Panel painting by Giotto on gold ground showing the Virgin in half length within an arched frame, wearing a deep blue mantle edged in gold over a green-lined veil, her head inclined; the Christ Child sits on her left arm in a white cloth, reaching with one hand for the white rose she holds up, while his other hand rests on the white cloth about his hips. Both haloes are tooled in the gold
caption: Madonna and Child, c. 1320. Tempera and gold on panel, 85.5 × 62 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection. Centre panel of a dispersed polyptych.

alt: Panel painting by Giotto on gold ground showing Saint Stephen in half length within an arched field. The young deacon, tonsured, with two pale stones resting on his head, wears a white dalmatic with richly patterned collar and an embroidered geometric panel on the breast; he turns his gaze to the left and holds a red, gold-ornamented book draped with a yellow and green cloth, one hand elegantly spread on its cover. The halo and the arch’s spandrels are tooled with floral ornament in the gold
caption: Saint Stephen, c. 1320–1325. Tempera and gold on panel, 84 × 54 cm. Florence, Museo Horne. Lateral panel of the dispersed polyptych reconstructed between Washington, Florence and Chaalis.

alt: Tall panel painting by Giotto on gold ground showing Saint John the Evangelist in half length under an arched field, with a gabled pinnacle above containing a half-length angel in red with multicoloured wings. The aged apostle, bald-crowned with a full grey beard, wears a blue tunic and rose mantle; he turns his gaze to the left while writing with a pen on a long unfurling scroll inscribed with lines of text, which he steadies with his other hand at its rolled lower end
caption: Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1320–1325. Tempera and gold on panel. Chaalis, Abbaye Royale, Musée Jacquemart-André (Institut de France). Lateral panel of the dispersed polyptych reconstructed between Washington, Florence and Chaalis, with its original gable of an angel.

alt: Tall panel painting by Giotto on gold ground showing Saint Lawrence in half length under an arched field, with a gabled pinnacle above containing a half-length angel in red with multicoloured wings. The young tonsured deacon faces nearly frontally, wearing a red dalmatic with a richly patterned collar and breast panel and a blue stole crossing his shoulder; he holds a tall green martyr’s palm upright in one hand and a green, gold-ornamented book against his body with the other.
caption: Saint Lawrence, c. 1320–1325. Tempera and gold on panel. Chaalis, Abbaye Royale, Musée Jacquemart-André (Institut de France). Lateral panel of the dispersed polyptych reconstructed between Washington, Florence and Chaalis, with its original gable of an angel.

alt: Wide gabled panel by Giotto on gold ground showing the death of the Virgin. Mary lies on an ornamented bier at the centre, surrounded by a dense crowd of mourning apostles, haloed figures and wing-folded angels; at the midpoint Christ stands holding a small swaddled figure, the Virgin’s soul, while an apostle bends to embrace her body and another kneels before the bier. Winged angels crowd the right-hand end of the scene
caption: The Entombment of Mary (Dormition of the Virgin), c. 1310. Tempera and gold on poplar panel, 75 × 179 cm. Berlin, Gemäldegalerie, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin. From the church of Ognissanti, Florence.

alt: Small gabled panel on gold ground showing the Crucifixion. Christ hangs on a tall cross at the centre, pale against the gold, with mourning angels flying around the cross arms, two catching his blood in cups. Below, a dense crowd divides at the cross: at the left the fainting Virgin is supported among the holy women while the kneeling Magdalen in red embraces the foot of the cross; at the right soldiers and onlookers with lances and shields gesture upward, one pointing in recognition.
caption: Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Crucifixion of Christ, c. 1315. Tempera and gold on panel, 56.4 × 33.7 cm. Berlin, Gemäldegalerie, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin.

alt: Gabled panel by Giotto: Saint Francis kneels on a rocky mountainside between two small chapels, receiving golden rays from a crucified Christ who appears above within crimson seraph wings; below, a three-part predella shows the Dream of Innocent III, the pope approving the Franciscan Rule, and Francis preaching to the birds
caption: Saint Francis of Assisi Receiving the Stigmata, with predella scenes of the Dream of Innocent III, the Approval of the Rule and the Sermon to the Birds, c. 1295–1300, tempera and gold on panel, 313 × 163 cm, inscribed OPUS IOCTI FLORENTINI. Paris, Musée du Louvre, inv. 309, from the church of San Francesco, Pisa.

alt: Five-panel altarpiece by Giotto in a Gothic-style frame: at the centre Christ crowns the kneeling Virgin, both in rose and white, while angels kneel before the throne; the four side panels hold dense ranks of gold-haloed saints and music-making angels; below, a predella with five bust medallions including the dead Christ at the centre
caption: Giotto di Bondone (and workshop), Coronation of the Virgin with Angels and Saints (Baroncelli Polyptych), c. 1328–1334, tempera and gold on panel, 185 × 323 cm, inscribed OPUS MAGISTRI JOCTI. Florence, Basilica di Santa Croce, Baroncelli Chapel.

alt: Five-panel cuspidate polyptych by Giotto on gold ground: at the centre the Virgin in deep blue sits on a white Gothic throne with the Child, the signature inscribed on the step; at the sides stand Saint Peter with keys, the archangel Gabriel with the Ave Maria scroll, Saint Michael in red wings spearing a dragon, and Saint Paul with sword and book; a predella below holds five roundels around the Man of Sorrows.
caption: Giotto di Bondone (and workshop), Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints Peter, Gabriel, Michael and Paul (Bologna Polyptych), c. 1330–1335, tempera and gold on panel, 91 × 340 cm, inscribed OPUS MAGISTRI IOCTI DE FLORENTIA. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, from the church of Santa Maria degli Angeli.

alt: Fresco in the Magdalen Chapel at Assisi: Christ, at the left with his apostles, stretches his arm toward Lazarus, who stands bound in white grave-wrappings at the door of a rock tomb, supported by onlookers who shield their faces; a kneeling woman adores at Christ's feet while two labourers remove the stone slab, all beneath a rocky landscape and dark sky
caption: Giotto di Bondone and workshop, The Raising of Lazarus, c. 1307–1309, fresco. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Lower Church, Magdalen Chapel, left wall, middle register.

alt: Fresco in the Magdalen Chapel at Assisi: Mary Magdalene in a red mantle kneels on rocky ground, reaching toward the risen Christ, who stands at the right in white robes within a radiance of gold rays, holding a long-handled implement; at the left two white-robed angels sit on the open pink marble sarcophagus, two more angels fly in the dark sky above a sparse hillside of trees.
caption: Giotto di Bondone and workshop, Noli me tangere, c. 1307–1309, fresco. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Lower Church, Magdalen Chapel, lunette of the left wall, above the Raising of Lazarus.

alt: Three-gabled side of Giotto's double-faced Stefaneschi Triptych: at the centre Christ enthroned in blue blesses amid angels, with the small kneeling Cardinal Stefaneschi at the throne's step; at the left Peter is crucified upside down between a pyramid and a white conical monument; at the right Paul is beheaded while Plautilla's veil descends from the sky; below, a predella with the enthroned Madonna, two censing angels and the twelve apostles
caption: Giotto di Bondone and assistants, Stefaneschi Triptych, recto: Christ Enthroned with Angels and Cardinal Jacopo Stefaneschi, between the Crucifixion of St Peter and the Beheading of St Paul; predella with the Madonna and Child Enthroned between Two Angels and the Twelve Apostles, c. 1315–1320, tempera and gold on poplar panel, central panel 178 × 89 cm (whole triptych c. 220 × 245 cm), modern gilded frames. Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana, inv. MV.40120.10, from the Basilica of Old St Peter's.

alt: Double-sided painted cross by Giotto from the Scrovegni Chapel: the pale dead Christ hangs against a blue field framed by gold damask panels within an elaborately carved and gilded mixtilinear frame; the blessing Redeemer occupies the polylobed summit above a red titulus, the praying Virgin and mourning Saint John the quatrefoil terminals, and the rock of Golgotha with Adam's skull the triangular foot
caption: Crucifix, c. 1304, tempera and gold on poplar panel, 223 × 164 cm. Padua, Musei Civici agli Eremitani, from the Scrovegni Chapel.

alt: Lunette fresco in the Peruzzi Chapel: within a Gothic marble baldachin, the aged priest Zacharias swings a censer at the draped altar of incense while the angel appears beside it; musicians and bystanders attend at the left, and at the right the waiting congregation stands beneath the loggia of the temple precinct; a grey-blue loss interrupts the lower right of the scene
caption: The Annunciation to Zacharias, c. 1310–1315, fresco and a secco, lunette of the left wall. Florence, Basilica di Santa Croce, Peruzzi Chapel.

alt: Fresco in the Peruzzi Chapel showing two rooms of one house: at the left the mute Zacharias, seated, writes the name of his son while women present the infant John to him; at the right Elizabeth rests in her curtained bed attended by three women; the architecture opens in section beneath a projecting upper storey
caption: The Birth and Naming of Saint John the Baptist, c. 1310–1315, fresco and a secco, middle register of the left wall. Florence, Basilica di Santa Croce, Peruzzi Chapel.

alt: Fresco in the Peruzzi Chapel: under a classical loggia crowned by statues and garlands against a dark sky, Herod sits at the banquet table as the Baptist's head is presented before him; at the left a young musician plays the vielle; at the right, in an adjoining room, the kneeling Salome offers the head on a dish to the seated Herodias
caption: The Feast of Herod, c. 1310–1315, fresco and a secco, lower register of the left wall. Florence, Basilica di Santa Croce, Peruzzi Chapel.

alt: Fresco lunette by Giotto showing Saint John asleep on the rocky island of Patmos, surrounded by the sea, while apocalyptic visions appear in the sky above: a white-clad figure seated on clouds holding a sickle, a winged dragon, and a reclining woman with a child. The surface is heavily abraded, with large losses at the left
caption: Saint John the Evangelist on Patmos, c. 1310–1315. Fresco and a secco, lunette. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Peruzzi Chapel, right wall.

alt: Fresco by Giotto showing Saint John the Evangelist, in an orange mantle, extending his right arm toward the widow Drusiana, who rises from her bier wrapped in grave clothes. Behind them stretch the crenellated walls, towers and domed buildings of Ephesus against a dark sky. Apostles stand at the left, a dense crowd of mourners at the right; two figures kneel at John’s feet
caption: The Raising of Drusiana, c. 1310–1315. Fresco and a secco. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Peruzzi Chapel, right wall.

alt: Fresco by Giotto showing Saint John the Evangelist rising bodily from his open grave inside a columned building shown in section, lifted on rays of light toward Christ, who leans down from a cloud of haloed figures to grasp him. Astonished witnesses stand at left and right beneath two balconied structures; a figure crouches by the empty tomb below
caption: The Ascension of Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1310–1315. Fresco and a secco. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Peruzzi Chapel, right wall.

alt: Fresco by Giotto showing Saint Francis kneeling on the rocky slope of La Verna, arms raised, as a crucified seraph with six red wings appears in the dark sky above; golden rays run from the seraph’s wounds to the saint’s hands, feet and side. A small chapel with a rose window stands at the right, a bird perches on the cliff at the upper left
caption: The Stigmatization of Saint Francis, c. 1325. Fresco. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, exterior wall above the entrance arch of the Bardi Chapel.

alt: Fresco lunette by Giotto showing the young Francis, naked to the waist and praying, wrapped in the blue mantle of the Bishop of Assisi at the right, while at the left his angry father, in a yellow robe and holding the clothes his son has shed, is restrained by a bystander. Two groups of onlookers, including women and children, flank a pink palace raised on a high masonry podium; a child at each edge reacts to the scene.
caption: Saint Francis Renouncing His Worldly Goods, c. 1325. Fresco, lunette. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Bardi Chapel, left wall.

alt: Fresco by Giotto showing the interior of a chapter house rendered in section, its three arched bays framed by slender columns under a red-tiled roof. Saint Francis appears at the centre, standing with arms raised in the form of a cross, visible only to some of the hooded friars seated on benches around the room; Saint Anthony of Padua stands preaching at the left
caption: The Apparition of Saint Francis at the Chapter of Arles, c. 1325. Fresco. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Bardi Chapel, left wall.

alt: Fresco by Giotto showing the dead Saint Francis laid on a bier, surrounded by friars who kneel to kiss his hands and feet, raise their arms in grief, or stand in silent mourning; clerics and a knight attend at the sides. Above, angels carry the saint’s soul to heaven in a mandorla of light against the blue sky. A large irregular loss, left as a neutral patch, interrupts the centre of the scene
caption: The Death and Ascension of Saint Francis, c. 1325. Fresco. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Bardi Chapel, left wall.

alt: Fresco lunette by Giotto showing the pope seated at the left under a coffered canopy crowned by a pediment with a bust medallion, while a standing mitred prelate in red holds out the scroll of the Rule to Saint Francis, who kneels before them at the head of a compact group of kneeling friars. Two pairs of standing figures in antique mantles frame the scene at the outer edges. Large plaster losses interrupt the upper left of the field.
caption: The Confirmation of the Franciscan Rule, c. 1325. Fresco, lunette. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Bardi Chapel, right wall.

alt: Fresco by Giotto showing the Sultan of Egypt enthroned at the centre on a tall marble throne against a green patterned hanging, one hand resting on his knee, while his priests retreat at the left, one hiding his face in an orange mantle, and Saint Francis stands at the right beside a blazing fire with a companion friar behind him
caption: Saint Francis before the Sultan (The Trial by Fire), c. 1325. Fresco. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Bardi Chapel, right wall.

alt: Heavily damaged fresco by Giotto, its centre lost to a vast neutral patch shaped like a vanished funerary monument. At the left a dying friar sits up in bed, drawing back a curtain as he sees the ascending Saint Francis; at the right the sleeping Bishop of Assisi receives the same vision in his bed. A fragment at the centre preserves a group of friars’ heads, and two mourning figures survive at the lower right
caption: The Visions of Fra Agostino and of Bishop Guido of Assisi, c. 1325. Fresco. Florence, Santa Croce, right transept, Bardi Chapel, right wall.

alt: Madonna with Child between Saint John the Baptist and Saint John the Evangelist
caption: Madonna with Child between Saint John the Baptist and Saint John the Evangelist, 1299, fresco, Palazzo dell'Opera della Primaziale Pisana, sala della Deputazione, Pisa.

alt: Circular marble relief within a plain raised rim, showing a crowned and veiled Virgin seated at the left with the Christ Child at the right; both figures are polished and fully carved while the ground behind them remains rough, and their feet project at the lower edge of the disc.
caption: Madonna and Child, marble tondo, c. 1265–1270. Originally destined for the sacristy wall of the pieve di Sant'Andrea, Empoli; transferred to the Museo della Collegiata at the end of the nineteenth century. Empoli, Museo della Collegiata di Sant'Andrea.

alt: Octagonal marble pulpit raised on nine columns, four of them standing on lions devouring their prey; trilobed arches span the intervals and the parapet above is carved with densely populated relief panels separated by standing figures, with an eagle lectern projecting at the right.
caption: Siena, Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta. Nicola Pisano with Arnolfo di Cambio, Lapo, Giovanni Pisano and workshop, Pulpit, contracted 29 September 1265, final payment 6 November 1268. Carrara marble with granite and porphyry columns. Originally beneath the dome to the right of the choir; dismantled in the early sixteenth century and re-erected in the present position by 1543, with Renaissance stair and bridge carved by Bernardino di Giacomo, 1536–1539, probably to a design by Baldassarre Peruzzi.

alt: Two-tiered polygonal marble fountain with carved reliefs, dusted with snow, standing before the crenellated Gothic façade of the Palazzo dei Priori in Perugia.
caption: Perugia, Piazza IV Novembre. Nicola and Giovanni Pisano, Fontana Maggiore, 1275–1278 (inscription dated 1278; bronze crown signed by Rubeus, 1277), seen from the south-east, with the flank and main portal of the Palazzo dei Priori (begun 1293) and, above the portal, the bronze griffin of Perugia and the Guelph lion.

alt: Marble sculpture of a crowned, veiled Virgin holding the Christ Child on her left arm; mother and child turn their heads toward one another, their faces meeting at close range, the drapery falling in long diagonal folds. Photographed in studio light against a dark ground.
caption: Madonna and Child, known as the Madonna del Colloquio, marble, c. 1290–1302. Originally on the external lunette of the western portal of the south transept, Pisa Cathedral; removed to the Camposanto in 1829, now Pisa, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Ministry of Culture catalogue image, ICCD 0900235648.

alt: Polychrome marble Gothic cathedral façade with three deeply splayed portals below and, above, a large circular window flanked by loggias, crowned by three gabled cusps filled with gold-ground mosaics; free-standing statues project from the wall at the level of the upper cornice and along the flanking turrets.
caption: Siena, Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta. West façade. Lower register by Giovanni Pisano, 1284–c. 1297, with the three splayed portals, lateral turrets, and the statue programme of prophets, patriarchs, sibyls, and philosophers (originals in the Museo dell'Opera della Metropolitana; the figures in situ are copies). Upper register attributed either to Camaino di Crescentino, c. 1299–1317, or to Giovanni di Cecco, after 1376. Cusp mosaics executed in Venice, 1878. White marble with red Siena marble and green serpentine of Prato.

alt: Eight over-lifesize weathered marble figures standing in a receding rank against a dark ground, lit obliquely from above: bearded and youthful men in heavy classical drapery, their necks long and heads thrust forward, several leaning markedly out from the hips.
caption: Giovanni Pisano, prophets, patriarchs, sibyls and philosophers from the lower façade of Siena Cathedral, marble, c. 1285–1297. Siena, Museo dell'Opera della Metropolitana, installation view from the head of the rank. The originals were withdrawn from the exterior and replaced by copies.

alt: Eight over-lifesize marble figures standing in a receding rank on a low plinth against a dark wall, lit from the right: the two nearest are pale and comparatively well preserved, while those behind are discoloured, deeply pitted and abraded. All lean forward from the hips with necks extended and heads carried in advance of the chest.
caption: Giovanni Pisano, eight prophets, patriarchs, sibyls and philosophers from the lower façade of Siena Cathedral, marble, c. 1284–1297. Siena, Museo dell'Opera della Metropolitana, installation view. The originals were removed from the façade and replaced by copies.

alt: Hexagonal white marble pulpit on slender columns, its parapet carved with five deeply undercut relief panels of crowded figures; lions and a crouching male figure support the columns at the base.
caption: Pistoia, Pieve di Sant'Andrea. Pulpit, 1298–1301 (dated by inscription "sub primo mille trigentis"). Marble. Hexagonal parapet with five narrative reliefs of the life of Christ, carried on seven columns resting on stylophore lions, a telamon, and a base of eagle, griffin, and winged lion.

alt: Deeply undercut marble relief: at the upper left a winged angel addresses a standing veiled woman, with a bearded man seated in thought below; across the centre a veiled Virgin reclines and reaches toward a swaddled infant in a manger, the heads of an ox and an ass leaning above; at the right angels and shepherds stand among trees with sheep and goats below; at the lower centre a woman pours water into a large footed basin while a seated woman holds a naked infant.
caption: Annunciation, Nativity and Annunciation to the Shepherds, first relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Sant'Andrea, Pistoia. Marble, 1298–1301. The Annunciation at the upper left with Joseph seated below; the reclining Virgin at the centre reaching toward the swaddled Child in the manger, with the ox and ass above; the Annunciation to the Shepherds and the flock at the right; the preparation of the Child's bath at the lower centre. The signature inscription is visible along the cornice at the lower right, beginning LAUDE DE TRI[NI].

alt: Marble relief packed edge to edge with violently contorted figures: a crowned man leans forward from a throne at the upper right; young soldiers in short tunics raise their arms to strike and wrench infants from women's grasp; mothers clutch living children or bend double over dead ones; small nude bodies lie heaped along the lower edge; at the upper centre one veiled woman has drawn her hands across her eyes.
caption: Massacre of the Innocents, third relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Sant'Andrea, Pistoia. Marble, 1298–1301. Herod enthroned at the upper right, the sole seated figure; the executioners in short tunics moving through the centre and left; the mothers filling the greater part of the field, shown simultaneously at every stage from seizure to bereavement; the slaughtered children heaped along the lower edge.

alt: Deeply undercut marble relief: the emaciated body of the crucified Christ at the centre, head fallen forward, feet set one above the other on a small ledge with a skull beneath; at the left a veiled woman collapses backward into the arms of her companions while a draped figure stands with bowed head beside the cross; below, a soldier drives a lance upward with both hands; at the right a dense crowd of bearded and youthful faces looks up, and an angel at the upper corner pushes a small nude figure downward.
caption: Crucifixion, fourth relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Sant'Andrea, Pistoia. Marble, 1298–1301. The dead Christ at the centre, feet crossed on a suppedaneum above the skull of Adam; at the left the Virgin collapses into the arms of the holy women with St John standing apart; below the cross Longinus drives the lance upward; at the right a crowd of individuated witnesses, and at the upper right an angel thrusting a small figure downward.

alt: Densely carved marble relief: a bearded Christ sits enthroned at the upper centre with arms opened and chest bared; directly below his feet two bowed figures raise a cross; at the left clothed figures stand in tiered ranks with half-nude figures rising along the lower edge; at the right nude bodies are seized and inverted by horned demons, a coiled serpent and a snouted beast filling the corner.
caption: Last Judgement, fifth relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Sant'Andrea, Pistoia. Marble, 1298–1301. Christ enthroned at the upper centre displaying the wounds; beneath his feet angels raise the Cross at the exact axis of the field; the Elect in ordered ranks at his right with the resurrecting dead below; the Damned seized by demons and beasts at his left, a serpent coiling among them.

alt: White marble eagle standing with wings raised and spread, head erect and turned to one side, talons grasping a book; a hexagonal bookrest with a projecting lower ledge rests across the raised wings. The plumage is carved in overlapping scale-like feathers on the breast and long striated flight feathers at the wing edges.
caption: Eagle lectern from the pulpit of Sant'Andrea, Pistoia, c. 1301, marble, Overall 70.5 × 61.5 × 40.6 cm; 93 kg. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

alt: Squared marble block carved on its face with a shallow recess: at the centre the dead Christ rises half-length from the tomb, head fallen forward on the chest, arms crossed at the wrists; two winged angels in short tunics stand at either side, each raising one arm to hold a cloth arched above his head, the right-hand angel steadying his forearm. The upper surface of the block is flat and framed by a narrow lip.
caption: Angel Pietà lectern from the pulpit of Sant'Andrea, Pistoia, c. 1300, marble, 44 × 45 × 36 cm; kg. 70, Berlin, Skulpturensammlung, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin.

alt: Circular marble pulpit on porphyry columns and carved figure-supports, its curved parapet densely carved with crowded relief scenes, an eagle lectern projecting at the upper right.
caption: Pisa, Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta. Pergamo, 1302–1310/11. Carrara marble, porphyry and marmo africano, h. 4.61 m. Dismantled after the fire of 1596 and reassembled in 1926; original location in the presbytery. View from the south-west, showing the convex narrative panels, the caryatid and telamon supports, the stylophorous lions and the eagle lectern.

alt: Marble statue of a crowned and veiled Virgin standing frontally, the Christ Child on her left arm turning his head back toward her and raising a hand to her shoulder; her mantle falls in long vertical folds gathered by a knotted cord, with traces of blue on the lining and gold on the hem and veil. The base is inscribed in Gothic letters. Behind rises a carved tomb with a recumbent effigy.
caption: Madonna and Child, c. 1305, marble with polychromy and gilding, 129 x 24 cm, Padua, Cappella degli Scrovegni.

alt: Three marble figures standing on a ledge above an altar: at the centre a crowned Virgin holding the Christ Child, who turns his head toward her; at either side a wingless young man in a long tunic with a vertical orphrey band, holding a tall candlestick. Behind and above, a recumbent effigy lies beneath a canopy whose curtains are drawn back by winged figures at the corners.
caption: Th entire group, c. 1305, marble with polychromy and gilding, Madonna: 129 x 24 cm; left candle-bearing deacon: 124 x 24 cm; right candle-bearing deacon: 126 x 24 cm, Cappella degli Scrovegni, Padua.

alt: Small marble statue of a crowned and veiled Virgin standing with the Christ Child held high on her left arm; her mantle is drawn across the body in a long diagonal ending in a broad gilded and fringed hem. The Child turns his head back toward her and reaches one arm up toward her crown.
caption: Madonna and Child, known as the Madonna della Cintola, marble with gilding, dated variously between c. 1300 and c. 1315, h. 69 cm. Prato, Cattedrale di Santo Stefano, Cappella del Sacro Cingolo, on the altar containing the relic of the Virgin's Girdle. The Child reaches toward his mother's crown, a gesture read as prefiguring the Coronation. Photographed before the statue's removal to the Opificio delle Pietre Dure, Florence, for restoration; its return to Prato is anticipated for 2027.

alt: Black-and-white photograph of three marble figures on a metal display mount: at the centre a woman in a pierced coif and wimple, head tilted back and eyes lifted, rising from a mass of drapery; at either side a figure bent steeply forward, face hidden within a deep hood, arms extended toward her.
caption: Elevatio of Margaret of Brabant, white Carrara marble, c. 1313. From the funerary monument commissioned by Henry VII for San Francesco di Castelletto, Genoa; dismembered before 1602, dispersed at the demolition of the church in the early nineteenth century, the "Elevatio corporis" rediscovered in 1874. Genoa, Museo di Sant'Agostino. H. c. 150 cm. Photographed on a modern metal mount by Paolo Monti (BEIC 6356347), before the restoration completed at the Opificio delle Pietre Dure in 2024.

alt: Three weathered marble figures standing in a shallow vaulted niche: at the left a gaunt bearded man in a shaggy fleece garment rests his hand on the head of a small kneeling figure with joined hands; at the centre a crowned and veiled woman on an inscribed plinth holds a headless child on her left arm; at the right a youthful figure holds a book against his chest.
caption: Madonna and Child between St John the Baptist and St John the Evangelist, with the donor Pietro, marble, 1300-06. From the lunette of the main portal of the Baptistery of San Giovanni, Pisa; now Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. The Baptist presents the kneeling donor at the left; the Evangelist holds his book at the right; the Madonna's base carries the inscription naming Peter as supervisor and Giovanni, son of Nicola, as sculptor.

alt: Small ivory figure of the crucified Christ, gold in colour with the head falling onto the right shoulder with eyes open beneath contracted brows, long striated hair framing a curled beard; the torso is attenuated with the ribcage sharply articulated, and a knotted loincloth falls in deep folds. The arms are broken away at the shoulders and the legs below the calf.
caption: Christ crucifié, elephant ivory with traces of gilding, Tuscany, 1270–1280, 20.5 x 6.3 cm. Made for a cross now lost; arms and lower legs missing. Paris, Musée de Cluny – Musée national du Moyen Âge, acquired 2023 as a work of major heritage interest, the first sculpture by Giovanni Pisano to enter a French public collection.

alt: Small ivory figure of the crucified Christ photographed against a grey ground: the head falls forward and to one side with eyes closed, long waved hair and a divided beard retaining traces of gilding; the torso is carved with sharply defined clavicles, ribs and abdominal channel; a loincloth knotted at the hip falls in broad planes broken by angular projecting folds. The arms are broken away at the shoulders and the legs below the knee.
caption: The Crucified Christ, carved elephant ivory with traces of gilding, 1290–1310. 15.3 x 6 x 5 cm. London, Victoria and Albert Museum.

alt: Polychrome wooden crucifix on a white wall: the emaciated body of Christ hangs with arms stretched steeply upward, head fallen forward and to one side with eyes closed, dark waved hair and divided beard; the loincloth is gilded with a green border, and the cream flesh shows extensive paint loss exposing a brown ground. The plain cross carries a red tablet lettered INRI, and the shaft ends in a metal socket.
caption: Crocifisso d'Elci, 1290–1299, polychrome wood, 87 x 47,5 cm, Pisa, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo.

alt: Polychromed wooden crucifix against a pale ground: the body of Christ hangs with arms stretched steeply upward, head fallen onto the right shoulder with eyes closed, long dark hair and a divided beard; the loincloth is reddish-brown with gilded edges. The cross is carved as a dark tree trunk with the stubs of cut branches, rising from a rocky mound at whose foot lies a skull, with a red titulus lettered in gold above the head.
caption: Crucifix, c. 1285, polychromed and gilded wood, h.: 114 cm (Cross); 71 cm (Christ), Siena, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo.

alt: Painted wooden crucifix set in a shallow white niche on a modern conical base: the body of Christ hangs with arms stretched taut, head fallen forward, the chest pulled upward and the abdomen hollowed; blood runs from the wound in the right side; the knees bend sharply so that the legs swing to one side, the feet set one above the other. The cross is a dark stripped trunk with evenly spaced branch-stubs along shaft and arms.
caption: Crucifix, carved and painted wood, c. 1300. H. 88 cm. From the Cathedral of San Cerbone; Massa Marittima, Museo di Arte Sacra.

alt: Small shaped wooden reliquary cross on a gold ground. The dead Christ hangs with bowed head and closed eyes. Helmeted soldiers stand on the left, one piercing his side with a lance, and a centurion in Roman armour raises his hand on the right. The mourning Virgin and St John stand in the side terminals. A haloed saint in a brown habit and dark veil kneels at the foot, kissing Christ's bleeding feet. At the top, a red panel carries a long Latin inscription in white Gothic letters above a glazed recess holding a small silver cross
caption: Reliquary Cross (recto): Christus patiens with the lance-bearer and the centurion, the Virgin, St John and a kneeling saint, c. 1290–1310. Tempera and gold on panel, punched decoration, glass cabochons; 45 × 28.3 cm. Spoleto, Museo Nazionale del Ducato di Spoleto (Rocca Albornoziana), inv. 1076; State property (Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria). From the female monastery of San Paolo inter vineas, Spoleto, later at Sant'Alò.

alt: Back of a small shaped reliquary cross on a gold ground. The dead Christ sags heavily from the cross, head fallen forward, beneath a red plaque inscribed INRI. Mary Magdalene and St Paul holding a sword stand on the left; St Peter with a red book and St John the Baptist stand on the right. The Virgin and St John the Evangelist occupy the side terminals. At the foot, St Francis in a brown habit kneels against the bleeding feet. At the top, two standing angels flank a small glazed compartment containing relics wrapped in white and red cloth
caption: Reliquary Cross (verso): Dead Christ with the Virgin, St John, St Mary Magdalene, St Paul, St Peter, St John the Baptist and St Francis; in the cimasa, a glazed relic compartment flanked by two angels. c. 1290–1310. Tempera and gold on panel, punched decoration, glass cabochons; 45 × 28.3 cm. Spoleto, Museo Nazionale del Ducato di Spoleto (Rocca Albornoziana), inv. 1076; State property (Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria). From the female monastery of San Paolo inter vineas, Spoleto, later at Sant'Alò.

alt: Large shaped wooden painted cross, damaged by fire and cut down. The dead Christ hangs with outstretched straight arms, head fallen on his right shoulder, eyes closed. He has a gaunt rib cage, a swollen belly and a bleeding side wound, and wears a bright red loincloth striped with black. The flanking panels and ground, originally silver, are now darkened and mottled. Small mourning figures of the Virgin and St John survive at the cut-down ends of the arms. Above, a red plaque bears a Latin inscription in white letters. In the broken top terminal, Christ in red robes blesses and holds a book within a blue mandorla, with an angel beside it. The lower end of the cross is largely bare wood
caption: Master of Sant'Alò (attributed), Painted Crucifix, c. 1290–1295. Tempera and silver on shaped panel, 190 × 129 cm. Trevi, Complesso museale di San Francesco, Raccolta d'arte (Pinacoteca, first floor). From the church of San Pietro in Pettine, near Trevi. Restored 1996 and 2013 (Coo.Be.C., Spoleto).

alt: Rectangular altarpiece on gold ground: Saint Cecilia enthroned at the centre in a rose robe and dark mantle, holding a book and a palm, flanked by eight scenes from her life in two registers — the wedding feast, her vow revealed to Valerian, the angelic crowning, her instruction of Valerian and Tiburtius, a baptism by Pope Urban, her preaching, her dispute before the prefect Almachius, and her martyrdom in the boiling bath
caption: Saint Cecilia and Stories from her Life, c. 1305–1310, tempera and gold on panel, 85 × 181 cm (whole panel), Florence, Galleria degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 no. 449.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing the young Francis, haloed and in a dark blue civilian mantle, walking through the main square of Assisi as a man kneels to spread his cloak on the ground before him. Behind rises the Roman temple of Minerva with six columns and a pediment containing a rose window, flanked by the civic tower at the left and a loggia-crowned building at the right. Two pairs of onlookers converse at the edges; a dark scar left by a lamp marks the blue sky.
caption: Attributed to Giotto di Bondone and workshop (this scene assigned by most critics to the Saint Cecilia Master), The Homage of a Simple Man in the Piazza of Assisi, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene I, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing a papal bedchamber built entirely of textiles under a coffered ceiling: a patterned canopy hangs from iron rods over the bed, before a wall of gold-diapered hanging edged with an embroidered valance. Pope Gregory IX lies asleep in his tiara and red mantle; beside the bed stands the haloed Saint Francis, drawing open his habit at the breast with his right hand and extending a small phial toward the pope with his left. Below, attendants sleep in varied postures, two of their faces effaced by old damage.
caption: Attributed to the Saint Cecilia Master and workshop, after the design of the Legend’s master, Saint Francis Appearing to Gregory IX in a Dream, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XXV, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing a night healing inside a canopied chamber: under a coffered ceiling on slender colonnettes, a checked curtain is looped aside to reveal a bed with a red coverlet where the wounded John of Lerida lies. The haloed Saint Francis bends over him, his hands at the man’s bandaged side; behind the bed attend two companions, one with dark outspread wings. At the left, beyond the curtain, three men — one in white, one in a violet mantle and cap, one in green — stand and converse, unaware of the miracle.
caption: Attributed to the Saint Cecilia Master and workshop, after the design of the Legend’s master, Saint Francis Healing the Wounded John of Lerida, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XXVI, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi showing a two-part miracle in a house rendered in section. At the upper left Saint Francis kneels on clouds before the half-figure of Christ, interceding. At the right, inside a tall chamber, the woman of Benevento, raised on her bier, sits up in her pale blue pall and makes her confession into the ear of a seated priest, while women marvel behind her and a servant and a lady attend at the bier’s foot; a small angel hovers above, and a dark winged demon flees across the centre. At the left, under a porch, clergy with candles and book and a group of friars look on.
caption: Attributed to the Saint Cecilia Master and workshop, after the design of the Legend’s master, The Confession of the Woman of Benevento Raised from the Dead, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XXVII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Fresco from the Upper Church at Assisi, the last of the cycle, showing Saint Francis flying down from the upper left through a blue sky toward a rose-coloured prison tower at the right, crowned by a tall column with spiral reliefs; the freed prisoner Peter steps out of its door, stretching his arms. At the centre two jailers examine the broken fetters; at the left the kneeling, mitred Bishop of Tivoli raises his hands in astonishment before a group of clergy and attendants, beside a white tiered tower. A dark timber structure with a ladder hangs suspended in the sky above.
caption: Attributed to the Saint Cecilia Master and workshop, after the design of the Legend’s master, Saint Francis Liberating the Prisoner Peter of Alife, Legend of Saint Francis, Scene XXVIII, c. 1290–1300. Fresco, c. 270 × 230 cm. Assisi, Basilica of San Francesco, Upper Church, nave.

alt: Gabled altarpiece: Saint Margaret of Antioch standing at the centre in a gold brocade mantle against a red cloth of honour, flanked by six scenes from her life in three registers — tending sheep at the encounter with Olibrius, her interrogation, her torture, the prison with the dragon seen through an iron grate, the torment by fire and water, and her beheading with angels bearing her soul to heaven
caption: Saint Margaret of Antioch and Stories from her Life, c. 1310s, tempera and gold on panel, Arcetri (Florence), church of Santa Margherita a Montici.

alt: Gabled panel on a stone church wall: the Virgin in a dark mantle enthroned frontally on a rose architectural throne, holding the Christ Child in red, with two half-length angels leaning over the throne back with long striped wings, and two small female saints standing at the lower corners

alt: Gabled panel: Saint Peter enthroned frontally in a green mantle and cross-marked pallium, blessing with his right hand and holding a book and a large gold key in his left, flanked by two standing angels resting their hands on the throne's arms, against a gold ground

alt: Gabled panel: half-length Virgin in a dark blue-green mantle with a gold star at the brow, holding the Christ Child in a pale translucent tunic who twists upward reaching for her mantle, two small inscribed plaques in the gold ground beside her head

alt: Gabled panel: the Virgin in a dark gold-edged mantle seated on a throne of red, white and green geometric inlay, holding the Christ Child in red who grasps a small bird, while Saint Francis kneels in prayer at the lower right

alt: Large panel in a gilded Gothic tabernacle frame: the Virgin in a dark mantle with a gold sunburst at the shoulder enthroned with the Christ Child in red, surrounded by six angels — four leaning on the throne, two below swinging censers — with a fifteenth-century Annunciation painted in the frame's upper spandrels
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Six Angels, c. 1315–1320, tempera and gold on panel, 230 × 150 cm, from the oratory of Santa Maria Maddalena at Pian di Mugnone; Florence, Museo di San Marco (on deposit at the Gallerie degli Uffizi); fifteenth-century frame attributed to the workshop of Bicci di Lorenzo, with the Annunciation in the spandrels.

alt: Gabled panel: the Virgin in a dark star-marked mantle seated on a throne with rose-red inlaid wings, holding the Christ Child in a pale tunic and translucent veil, who displays an inscribed Latin scroll and bears a red cross in his halo
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned, c. 1315, tempera and gold on panel, Florence, Galleria dell’Accademia; provenance unknown, formerly on deposit at Pescia.

alt: Triptych of three gabled gold-ground panels: at the centre the Virgin in a dark mantle cradles the Christ Child, wrapped in translucent white, almost horizontally in both arms as he reaches up toward her; on the left a veiled female saint holds a red book, on the right a female saint holds a martyr's palm
caption: Master of Saint Cecilia (the “Master of the Horne Triptych”), Madonna and Child between Two Female Saints, 1310s, tempera and gold on panel, 120 × 160 cm (overall), Florence, Museo Horne.

alt: Arched detached fresco in a gilded frame: the crowned Virgin with a great rayed halo and white veil, in rose-red robes, holds the Christ Child across her lap as he twists away raising his right hand in blessing, while two angels behind hold up a red and green lozenge-patterned cloth of honour against a dark blue ground
caption: Master of Saint Cecilia (attributed), Madonna delle Grazie (Madonna and Child with Two Angels), c. 1313(?), detached fresco, Florence, Oratorio di Santa Maria delle Grazie, Lungarno Diaz; from the tabernacle on the first pier of the Ponte Rubaconte, later called Ponte alle Grazie after this image.
