alt: Hexagonal marble pulpit raised on granite columns, three of them standing on carved lions; round-headed trefoil arches span the supports, and the parapet above carries deeply carved relief panels of crowded figures, with an eagle lectern projecting at the upper right.
caption: Pisa, Battistero di San Giovanni. Pulpit, begun c. 1255–1257, completed 1259 (dated 1260 in Pisan style by the metrical inscription at the foot of the Last Judgement). Marble with red granite columns. Hexagonal cassa with five christological reliefs, the sixth face open for access; seven columns, three of them on stylophore lions, the central one on a figured pedestal; eagle lectern.

alt: Densely carved marble relief in which a veiled Virgin reclines across the centre of the field, her head raised on one hand; above and behind her the swaddled Child lies in a manger with the ox and ass, angels and a shepherd appear at the right among trees, two women bathe an infant in a basin at the lower centre, a bearded Joseph sits in thought at the lower left, and sheep and goats fill the lower right corner.
caption: Nativity, first relief of the parapet of the pulpit of the Baptistery of San Giovanni, Pisa. Marble, completed 1259 (dated 1260 in Pisan style). Four episodes in a single field: the Annunciation at the upper left, the Nativity with the reclining Virgin at the centre, the Annunciation to the Shepherds at the upper right, and the Bath of the Child at the lower centre, with Joseph seated at the lower left.

alt: High-relief marble panel: three horses crowd the left edge, their heads foreshortened; at the centre the Magi press forward, two kneeling with bowed heads and one standing; at the right the veiled Virgin sits enthroned with the Child leaning forward from her lap, a bearded Joseph at the far edge.
caption: Adoration of the Magi, second relief of the parapet of the pulpit of the Baptistery of San Giovanni, Pisa. White Carrara marble, h. 85 cm, completed 1259 (dated 1260 in Pisan style). The enthroned Virgin at the right derives from the figure of Phaedra on a second-century Roman sarcophagus then standing in the Piazza dei Miracoli, now in the Camposanto Monumentale.

alt: Crowded marble relief before an architectural skyline of arcades and gables: at the left a veiled woman advances with one hand raised; at the centre a slender column supports an altar; to the right a bearded elder holds a swaddled infant against his breast, with a dense press of heads behind him and a second bearded figure at the right edge.
caption: Presentation in the Temple, third relief of the parapet of the pulpit of the Baptistery of San Giovanni, Pisa. White Carrara marble, completed 1259 (dated 1260 in Pisan style). The aged priest supported by a youth derives from a Dionysus group on a Dionysiac relief vase, the so-called Vaso del Talento, then in the Piazza dei Miracoli and now in the Camposanto Monumentale.

alt: High-relief marble panel dominated by the nude body of the crucified Christ at its centre, arms outstretched and head fallen to one side; at the left a compact group of veiled women supports the swooning Virgin, while at the right a dense crowd of individuated male heads gesture upward toward the cross, angels leaning in from the upper corners.
caption: Crucifixion, fourth relief of the parapet of the pulpit of the Baptistery of San Giovanni, Pisa. White Carrara marble, completed 1259 (dated 1260 in Pisan style). The crucified Christ divides the field between the mourning women at the left and the agitated crowd of soldiers and witnesses at the right, with angels leaning inward at the upper corners and a skull at the foot of the cross.

alt: Densely packed marble relief: Christ enthroned at the upper centre with one hand raised, surrounded by tiered ranks of clothed figures to the left and a tumult of nude bodies seized by demons to the right, with figures rising from the ground along the bottom edge; a band of incised Latin lettering runs beneath the panel.
caption: Last Judgement, fifth relief of the parapet of the pulpit of the Baptistery of San Giovanni, Pisa. White Carrara marble, completed 1259 (dated 1260 in Pisan style). Christ enthroned in the upper centre with the wound displayed; the Elect in ordered ranks at his right, the Damned seized by demons at his left, the resurrection of the dead along the lower register. The signed and dated metrical inscription runs along the moulding beneath the relief.

alt: Octagonal marble pulpit raised on nine columns, four of them standing on lions devouring their prey; trilobed arches span the intervals and the parapet above is carved with densely populated relief panels separated by standing figures, with an eagle lectern projecting at the right.
caption: Siena, Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta. Nicola Pisano with Arnolfo di Cambio, Lapo, Giovanni Pisano and workshop, Pulpit, contracted 29 September 1265, final payment 6 November 1268. Carrara marble with granite and porphyry columns. Originally beneath the dome to the right of the choir; dismantled in the early sixteenth century and re-erected in the present position by 1543, with Renaissance stair and bridge carved by Bernardino di Giacomo, 1536–1539, probably to a design by Baldassarre Peruzzi.

alt: Densely carved marble relief: at the upper left two women meet before a small gabled building; across the centre a veiled Virgin reclines on a thick mattress, her head inclined downward, with the swaddled Child in a manger above her flanked by the heads of an ox and an ass; angels and shepherds occupy the right, two kneeling women bathe a standing nude infant in a basin at the lower centre, a bearded Joseph sits at the lower left, and sheep and goats fill the lower right corner.
caption: Nicola Pisano and workshop (Arnolfo di Cambio, Lapo, Giovanni Pisano), Visitation and Nativity, first relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Siena Cathedral. Carrara marble, contracted 29 September 1265, completed 1268. The Visitation at the upper left before a Gothic aedicule; the reclining Virgin at the centre with the swaddled Child, ox and ass above; the Annunciation to the Shepherds at the right; the Bath of the Child at the lower centre; Joseph seated at the lower left. The tall draped figures at either edge belong to the parapet's angle articulation.

alt: Crowded marble relief filled with horses and camels seen at varying angles, their heads crowded together and dogs running beneath their hooves; grooms move among them, a broad tree rises at the centre, and at the upper right a veiled and crowned Virgin sits enthroned with the Child as a bearded man bows before her and a second figure presents a covered vessel.
caption: Nicola Pisano and workshop (Arnolfo di Cambio, Lapo, Giovanni Pisano), Journey and Adoration of the Magi, second relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Siena Cathedral. Carrara marble, contracted 29 September 1265, completed 1268. The retinue of horses, camels and dogs occupies the lower two-thirds of the field; the enthroned Virgin and Child receive the offering of the Magi at the upper right. The standing draped figures at the left edge belong to the parapet's angle articulation.

alt: Densely carved marble relief: at the left a veiled woman holds two birds beside a bearded elder who receives an infant, before a small Gothic canopied building; ranks of bearded and mitred heads fill the centre and upper right; at the lower right a veiled woman sits sidesaddle holding a child and turns her head backward, with the head of an ass at the panel's edge.
caption: Nicola Pisano and workshop (Arnolfo di Cambio, Lapo, Giovanni Pisano), Presentation in the Temple and Flight into Egypt, third relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Siena Cathedral. Carrara marble, contracted 29 September 1265, completed 1268. At the left the Virgin brings the two turtledoves of the purification offering and Simeon receives the Child before a Gothic ciborium standing for the Temple; at the right the Virgin rides sidesaddle with the Child, turning back toward the scene she leaves, with Joseph and the ass beyond.

alt: Marble relief packed edge to edge with struggling figures: a crowned man sits enthroned at the upper left; below and to the right, young soldiers in short tunics raise their arms and seize infants; veiled women crouch and clutch children at the left; small nude bodies lie heaped along the bottom of the panel.
caption: Nicola Pisano and workshop (Arnolfo di Cambio, Lapo, Giovanni Pisano), Massacre of the Innocents, fourth relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Siena Cathedral. Carrara marble, contracted 29 September 1265, completed 1268. Herod enthroned at the upper left; the executioners in short tunics at the centre and right; the mothers grouped at the left; the slaughtered children heaped along the lower edge. The standing figure at the left of the image belongs to the parapet's angle articulation.

alt: Marble relief filled edge to edge with figures: the crucified Christ at the centre with head fallen forward and a small skull at the foot of the cross; at the left a veiled woman collapses into the arms of her companions while a draped figure raises a hand to his face in grief; at the right a dense crowd of bearded and youthful heads gestures upward; at the upper left a standing figure holds a miniature domed building.
caption: Nicola Pisano and workshop (Arnolfo di Cambio, Lapo, Giovanni Pisano), Crucifixion, fifth relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Siena Cathedral. Carrara marble, contracted 29 September 1265, completed 1268. The crucified Christ at the centre with the titulus above and the skull of Adam at the foot; the swooning Virgin among the holy women and the mourning St John at the left; a dense press of witnesses and soldiers at the right; a figure bearing an architectural model at the upper left, as yet unidentified.

alt: Marble relief packed with some forty individuated heads in four tiered ranks: crowned and veiled figures at the top with hands raised in prayer; densely crowded bearded and youthful faces in the middle; and half-nude figures rising from the lower edge, one woman holding a child at the right.
caption: Nicola Pisano and workshop (Giovanni Pisano, Arnolfo di Cambio, Goro, Lapo and Donato di Ricevuto), The Elect, sixth relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Siena Cathedral. Carrara marble, contracted 29 September 1265, completed 1268. Four tiered ranks of the blessed, crowned and clothed above, with the half-nude resurrected rising along the lower edge. The Last Judgement is divided across this panel and the following one, with Christ the Judge at the angle between them.

alt: Marble relief crowded edge to edge: winged angels at the upper left incline toward a mass of clothed, bearded figures whose faces show bewilderment and pleading; toward the right the order collapses into nude bodies seized and carried head downward by horned, snouted demons, while at the lower edge figures crouch and crawl with their heads in their hands.
caption: Nicola Pisano and workshop (Giovanni Pisano, Arnolfo di Cambio, Goro, Lapo and Donato di Ricevuto), The Damned, seventh relief of the parapet of the pulpit of Siena Cathedral. Carrara marble, contracted 29 September 1265, completed 1268. Angels at the upper left; the judged, still clothed, in the central registers; demons seizing and inverting the nude damned at the right and along the lower edge. The Last Judgement is divided across this panel and the preceding one, with Christ the Judge at the angle between them.

alt: Tiered white marble funerary monument standing on an altar within a richly hung chapel: a densely carved narrative sarcophagus at its centre, a scaled lid above bearing standing saints, and a tall pinnacle crowned by a blessing figure; two kneeling angels holding candlesticks flank the base.
caption: Bologna, Basilica di San Domenico, Cappella dell'Arca. Arca di San Domenico. Central sarcophagus by Nicola Pisano and workshop (Arnolfo di Cambio, Lapo di Ricevuto, Guglielmo da Pisa), commissioned 1264, completed 1267, with six high-relief panels of the life of the saint separated by six statuettes; originally borne on caryatid figures, since removed. Cimasa and crowning statues by Niccolò dell'Arca from 1469; St Petronius, St Proculus and the candle-bearing angel by Michelangelo, 1494–95; predella by Alfonso Lombardi, 1532; altar frontal by Giovanni Battista Boudard to a design by Carlo Bianconi, 1768.

alt: Two-tiered polygonal marble fountain with carved reliefs, dusted with snow, standing before the crenellated Gothic façade of the Palazzo dei Priori in Perugia.
caption: Perugia, Piazza IV Novembre. Nicola and Giovanni Pisano, Fontana Maggiore, 1275–1278 (inscription dated 1278; bronze crown signed by Rubeus, 1277), seen from the south-east under snow, with the flank and main portal of the Palazzo dei Priori (begun 1293) and, above the portal, the bronze griffin of Perugia and the Guelph lion.

alt: Weathered marble relief filling a semicircular lunette: the lifeless body of Christ slumps diagonally from the cross into the arms of a bearded man who takes its weight; at the lower right another kneels and works at the feet with pincers; at the left a veiled woman draws the released hand to her cheek, with a file of veiled mourners behind her.
caption: Nicola Pisano, Deposition from the Cross, marble, c. 1257–1260. Lunette of the left portal — the portale della Croce of the façade portico, Cathedral of San Martino, Lucca. Christ's body slumps into the arms of Joseph of Arimathea as Nicodemus draws the nail from the feet with pincers; at the left the Virgin presses the released hand to her face, with the holy women behind her. Executed in the years of the Pisa Baptistery pulpit, completed 1260.

alt: Gothic triptych on gold ground by Allegretto Nuzi and Puccio di Simone, 1354: the Virgin in a blue mantle enthroned with the Christ Child holding a goldfinch, surrounded by eighteen angels and four saints; on the left wing Saint Anthony Abbot in a brown habit with staff; on the right wing the young Saint Venantius with a banner, in a red-gold brocade tunic and blue cloak; Crucifixion and Annunciation in the pinnacles
caption: Allegretto Nuzi and Puccio di Simone, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints and Angels, and Saints Anthony Abbot and Venantius, 1354, tempera and gold on panel, Left panel: 123.8 x 45.7 x 8.3 cm (framed); Middle panel: 150.5 x 66.7 x 8.3 cm (framed); Right panel: 123.8 x 43.2 x 8.3 cm (framed); Washington D.C., National Gallery of Art, inv. 1937.1.6.a–c.

alt: Gothic triptych on gold ground by Allegretto Nuzi, 1365: in the centre the Virgin in a dark blue mantle enthroned before a red cloth of honour, holding the blessing Christ Child, with small kneeling donors at the foot of the throne and a signed inscription along the base; on the left wing the Archangel Michael in armour with sword and shield trampling a dragon; on the right wing Saint Ursula in a rose gown and dark mantle holding a white banner with a red cross and the palm of martyrdom
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned between Saint Michael the Archangel and Saint Ursula, 1365, tempera and gold on panel, 123 x 65.8 cm; left side panel: 91.3 x 41.8 cm; right side panel: 92 x 41.4 cm, Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana, MV.40204.0.0.

alt: Gothic polyptych on gold ground by Allegretto Nuzi, 1366, in five pointed compartments: in the centre the Virgin in a dark mantle over a red gown, enthroned on a pink marble throne, holding the Christ Child in a yellow tunic, with a small Crucifix in the gable; on the left Saint Catherine, crowned, in pink, with palm and wheel, and Saint Francis in a brown habit showing the stigmata and holding a cross; on the right Saint Martin in a yellow tunic cutting his red cloak with a sword for a small half-naked beggar, and Saint Lucy in yellow and lilac holding a burning lamp and a palm; small half-length Franciscan saints in the side gables
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned between Saints Catherine of Alexandria, Francis of Assisi, Martin and Lucy, 1366, tempera and gold on panel, Apiro (Macerata), Palazzo Comunale, Sala Consiliare.

alt: Gothic panel by Allegretto Nuzi, 1366: the Virgin of Humility seated low on a large red cushion with gold pattern and tassels, nursing the Christ Child held in her arms; she wears a dark blue mantle decorated with gold vine leaves and grapes over a red gown patterned in gold; a crown of twelve dark stars surrounds her head, a crescent moon lies at her feet, and a cusped arch in raised gilding frames the scene on a gold ground; a damaged inscription runs along the lower edge
caption: Madonna of Humility (after the 2022 restoration), 1366, tempera and gold on panel, 164.5 × 125 cm, San Severino Marche, Pinacoteca Civica P. Tacchi Venturi, from the church of San Domenico, San Severino Marche.

alt: Gothic panel by Allegretto Nuzi, 1372, with a pointed top: the crowned Virgin seated frontally on a pale throne draped with a white patterned cloth, wearing a red gown with gold motifs and a dark mantle covered with gold palmettes; the Christ Child, in a gold tunic with blue sleeves and a blue sash, stands on her lap and touches her cheek while looking out at the viewer; a cusped arch in raised gilding frames the scene on a gold ground, and a signed inscription runs along the base of the throne
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned, 1372, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 167 × 96 cm, Urbino, Galleria Nazionale delle Marche, inv. D24.

alt: Small gabled panel by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground: the crowned Virgin in a red gown and a dark mantle with gold ornament, seated before a red and gold brocade cloth of honour, holding the Christ Child in a blue tunic who reclines across her lap with his hand at his mouth and a small bird; on the left Saint Bartholomew, bearded, holding a knife and a red book; on the right Saint Catherine, crowned, in yellow and orange, holding a palm; inscriptions on the step of the throne and along the base
caption: Virgin and Child Enthroned between Saints Bartholomew and Catherine of Alexandria, c. 1350–70, tempera and gold on panel, 51.5 × 28.2 cm, Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, inv. 1076.

alt: Small gabled panel by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground: Christ dead on the Cross with blood flowing from his wounds down to a rock where a skull lies; Mary Magdalene in red kneels and kisses his feet; the Virgin in a dark mantle stands on the left and Saint John in a blue tunic and pink mantle on the right; above the red titulus INRI the top of the Cross sprouts leaves, and a pelican feeds its young with its blood in a nest in the gable
caption: The Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint John the Evangelist and Mary Magdalene, c. 1350–70, tempera and gold on panel, 51.5 × 28.2 cm, Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, inv. 1078.

alt: Small portable triptych by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground with hinged wings: in the centre Christ on the Cross between the Virgin in blue and Saint John, with Mary Magdalene in red kneeling and embracing the Cross and a Dominican saint presenting a small kneeling woman in green; the blessing Christ in the gable; on the left wing Saint Francis in a brown habit and a bearded saint with staff and red book; on the right wing a bearded saint with book and knife and a female saint in yellow with palm and red cross; the Archangel Gabriel and the Virgin Annunciate in quatrefoils in the wing gables
caption: Portable Triptych with the Crucifixion, Saints and the Annunciation, 1350–55, tempera and gold on poplar panel, original frame; left wing 47.2 × 12.8 cm, central panel 47.2 × 25.2 cm, right wing 47.3 × 12.6 cm, Bern, Kunstmuseum, bequest of Adolf von Stürler, Versailles, inv. G 0198.

alt: Gothic polyptych by Allegretto Nuzi with five half-length figures on gold ground under cusped arches, in a gilded frame with pinnacles and twisted columns: in the centre the Virgin in a dark mantle and red gown tenderly holding the Christ Child, who holds a goldfinch; on the left Saint Mary Magdalene in red with long hair and an ointment jar, and Saint James with a book and a pilgrim's staff; on the right the young deacon Saint Stephen in a patterned gold dalmatic with palm and red book, and a bearded bishop saint with mitre and crozier, blessing; the names of the figures are inscribed on the base
caption: Virgin and Child, with Saints Mary Magdalene, James the Greater, Stephen, and a Bishop Saint, c. 1346, tempera, silver and tooled gold on panel; central panel 72.1 × 41.9 cm, side panels 60 × 29.8 cm each, Philadelphia Museum of Art, John G. Johnson Collection, 1917, inv. Cat. 5.

alt: Small gabled panel by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground: the Virgin in a dark mantle with gold ornament and a red gown, enthroned frontally on a tall red throne with gilded pinnacles, holding the standing Christ Child in a yellow tunic; behind the throne Saint Lucy holding a burning lamp and a female saint with a palm; in front Saint John the Baptist in a pink mantle with his hand on his breast and Saint Anthony Abbot in a black habit with staff and red book; the Archangel Gabriel in half-length in the gable
caption: Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints Lucy, John the Baptist and Anthony Abbot, a Female Martyr, and the Annunciate Angel, c. 1350, tempera and tooled gold on panel, 43.5 × 23.5 cm, Philadelphia Museum of Art, John G. Johnson Collection, 1917, inv. Cat. 2.

alt: Small rectangular panel by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground: the Virgin in half-length, her head inclined, wearing a dark mantle with fine gold lines and an embroidered border over a gold gown patterned with dark flowers, holds the Christ Child on her left arm; the Child, wrapped in a red and gold cloth, looks out at the viewer; both have finely punched haloes, and painted ornaments decorate the corners of the gold ground
caption: Virgin and Child, c. 1360, tempera, silver and tooled gold on panel with horizontal grain, 43.5 × 34.9 × 3.8 cm (framed), Philadelphia Museum of Art, John G. Johnson Collection, 1917, inv. Cat. 119.

alt: Small diptych by Allegretto Nuzi in gilded frames: on the left the Virgin in half-length, in a dark mantle with a gold border and a red gown, holding the Christ Child in a pink tunic who holds a goldfinch and turns toward her; on the right the dead Christ in half-length rising from a red tomb, with head bowed, eyes lowered and arms crossed over his breast, his hands and side bleeding and his body marked by the scourging; both on gold grounds with punched decorative borders
caption: Virgin and Child; Man of Sorrows, c. 1366, tempera and tooled gold on panel, 39 × 50.8 cm (overall), Philadelphia Museum of Art, John G. Johnson Collection, 1917, inv. Cat. 118.

alt: Gabled panel by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground in a frame with crockets: Christ dead on the Cross between two small mourning angels; Mary Magdalene in red kneels and embraces the foot of the Cross on a rocky ground; the Virgin in a dark mantle over a red gown stands on the left with hands joined, and Saint John in a red mantle over a green tunic stands on the right with head bowed; in the gable a pelican feeds its young in a green nest above the red titulus
caption: Allegretto Nuzi (attr.), The Crucifixion, c. 1345–50, tempera and gold on panel, 58.42 × 23.5 cm (unframed), 77.47 × 40.64 cm (framed), Richmond, Virginia Museum of Fine Arts, Arthur and Margaret Glasgow Fund, inv. 59.4.

alt: Small Gothic tabernacle by Allegretto Nuzi in an elaborate gilded frame with pinnacles and twisted columns: in the centre the Virgin enthroned under a canopy with a starry vault, holding the Christ Child, flanked by two angels, Saint John the Baptist and a female saint; on the left wing the Nativity with the ox and ass, Joseph and a choir of angels, and above an angel announcing to a shepherd; on the right wing the Crucifixion with the fainting Virgin, holy women, Saint John and Mary Magdalene in red at the foot of the Cross; the Annunciation divided between the gables of the wings; coats of arms on the base
caption: Madonna and Child with Saints, Crucifixion and Nativity, c. 1350–70, tempera and gold on panel, 77.5 × 53.3 × 12.7 cm (overall), Detroit Institute of Arts, Gift of James E. Scripps, inv. 89.19.

alt: Gothic triptych by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground: in the centre Christ in a blue tunic and golden mantle crowning the Virgin, who bows with hands crossed in a white patterned mantle, both seated on a throne draped in red with a green pattern, with four kneeling angels in blue and yellow playing instruments below; in the side panels crowds of haloed saints and prophets turned toward the centre, including Saint Francis in a brown habit on the left and Saint John the Baptist with a scroll and Saint Peter with keys and a book on the right; two small adoring angels in trefoils in the side gables
caption: The Coronation of the Virgin, c. 1360, tempera and gold on panel, Southampton City Art Gallery, purchased in 1951 through the Frederick William Smith Bequest Fund, inv. SOTAG 1403.

alt: Two gabled panels by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground, each filled with rows of haloed saints: on the left Mary Magdalene in red with the palm and Saint Lawrence in a white dalmatic holding a palm and his iron grill, with the crowned Saint Elizabeth of Hungary carrying roses in her skirt, a Franciscan friar and female saints above them; on the right Saint Louis of Toulouse in a mitre and a blue mantle covered with gold fleurs-de-lis holding a crozier, Saint Catherine beside him, and above them Saint Paul, Saint Jerome in a red cardinal's hat, Saint Dominic and Saint Ursula; pairs of angels at the top of each panel
caption: Saints and Angels, c. 1370, tempera and gold leaf on wood, 107.9 × 50.9 cm each, Houston, The Museum of Fine Arts, The Edith A. and Percy S. Straus Collection, inv. 44.568–.569.

alt: Gothic pentaptych by Allegretto Nuzi with five half-length figures on gold ground under pointed arches: in the centre the Virgin in a dark mantle and a red gown with gold stars holding the Christ Child, who has his hand at his mouth; on the left Mary Magdalene in red with an ointment jar and the young Saint John the Evangelist holding an open book with Latin text; on the right the bearded Saint Bartholomew with a knife and a book and the young Saint Venantius with a white banner; in the gables a Crucifix in the centre and small roundels with the mourning Virgin, Saint John, Saint Anthony Abbot and a female saint with a palm
caption: Madonna and Child with Saints Mary Magdalene, John the Evangelist, Bartholomew and Venantius, 1360s, tempera and gold on panel, c. 113–118 × 200–202 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli" (property of the Curia vescovile of Fabriano-Matelica).

alt: Three Gothic panels by Allegretto Nuzi joined in one frame, with full-length saints on gold ground above a red floor: in the centre Saint Augustine, bearded, in a mitre and a blue cope with gold patterns over a black habit, holding a crozier and an open book; on the left Saint Nicholas of Tolentino in a black habit holding a lily and a red book; on the right the young deacon Saint Stephen in a white dalmatic decorated with blue and red motifs, holding a palm and a red book
caption: Saint Augustine between Saint Nicholas of Tolentino and Saint Stephen, 1360s–early 1370s, tempera and gold on panel, c. 117–118 × 137–139 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli", from the sacristy of Saint Augustine.

alt: Half-length panel of Saint Bartholomew, bearded with dark hair, glancing to the right, holding a flaying knife and a red book, wearing a yellow tunic and violet mantle against a gold ground with a punched halo; attributed to Allegretto Nuzi, c. 1350, Orvieto, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo
caption: Saint Bartholomew the Apostle, c. 1350, tempera and gold on panel, Orvieto, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo.

alt: Small gabled panel by Allegretto Nuzi on a worn gold ground showing red underlayer: Christ on the Cross with four dark-winged angels around him holding bowls to catch his blood; Mary Magdalene in red kneels and embraces the foot of the Cross; on the left the Virgin supported by holy women; on the right Saint John in a pink mantle over a green tunic looking up; at the top a pelican feeding its young in a nest above a green tree growing from the Cross
caption: The Crucifixion, 1355–60, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 43.5 × 20 cm, New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975, inv. 1975.1.106.

alt: Long horizontal panel by Allegretto Nuzi with five half-length apostles on gold ground, each under a round gilded arch on twisted columns: from left, a bald bearded apostle in an ochre mantle holding a red book; a young apostle in a red mantle raising his hand and holding a green book; a bearded apostle holding a large knife and a red book, in a patterned tunic and lilac mantle; a young apostle in a blue tunic and red mantle holding a dark book; and Saint Peter, grey-bearded and tonsured, holding a large key and a book, with a white band marked with black crosses over an orange mantle
caption: Five Apostles in Half-Length, fragment of a predella, c. 1360, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 35.3 × 135.5 cm, Strasbourg, Musée des Beaux-Arts, inv. MBA 168; 44.R.20.

alt: Small panel by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground with a punched floral border: the Virgin in half-length, in a white veil and a dark mantle with a gold border and a large radiant gold star on the shoulder, over a red gown, looks out at the viewer with her right hand raised before her breast; on her left arm she holds the Christ Child in a pale tunic with a dark sash, who reaches toward her neckline and turns his head toward the viewer
caption: Allegretto Nuzi and workshop, Madonna and Child, c. 1365, tempera and gold on panel, 34.6 × 19.9 cm, Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana, inv. MV.40208.0.0.

alt: Small panel by Allegretto Nuzi and workshop on gold ground with a punched floral border: the dead Christ in half-length, naked to below the waist, with head bowed, eyes closed and long dark hair falling onto his shoulders; his arms are crossed over his breast, and red streams of blood flow from the wounds in his hands and side; a punched halo surrounds his head
caption: Allegretto Nuzi and workshop, Man of Sorrows (Vir dolorum), c. 1365, tempera and gold on panel, 34.8 × 20.3 cm, Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana, inv. MV.40210.0.0.

alt: Small Gothic panel on gold ground with a painted foliate border: the Virgin in a dark blue mantle and red gown enthroned under a pointed canopy with a starry blue vault, holding the Christ Child in a pink tunic; two angels in blue above the throne; on the left Saint Catherine, crowned, in a dark mantle, holding a palm and a large wheel; on the right Saint John the Baptist in a camel skin and pink mantle, barefoot, pointing and holding an inscribed scroll
caption: School of Allegretto Nuzi, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Angels between Saints Catherine of Alexandria and John the Baptist, c. 1380–90, tempera and gold on panel, 36.4 × 28.7 cm, Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana, inv. MV.40209.0.0.

alt: Small rectangular panel by Allegretto Nuzi on a worn gold ground showing red underlayer: Christ dead on the Cross above a dark mound; Mary Magdalene in orange-red kneels, embraces the Cross and presses her face to his feet; on the left the Virgin in a dark mantle with a gold star looks up with her hand at her throat; on the right Saint John in a pink mantle over a dark green tunic stands with hands clasped and head bowed
caption: Crucifixion with the Virgin Mary, Saint John the Evangelist and Saint Mary Magdalene, c. 1365, tempera and gold on panel, painted surface 23.3 × 15.7 cm, frame 34.9 × 27.3 × 7.3 cm, Birmingham (Alabama), Birmingham Museum of Art, Gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation, inv. 1961.113.

alt: Arched gold-ground panel with two standing saints on green ground, named on black tablets above: on the left Saint Catherine, crowned, in a pale pink gown with small patterns, holding a red book and resting her hand on a large spiked wheel; on the right Saint Bartholomew, bearded, in a light blue tunic and a white mantle with rosettes and red lining, holding a black book and a large knife; both turn toward the left
caption: Allegretto Nuzi and Francescuccio Ghissi, Saints Catherine and Bartholomew, c. 1350, tempera on wood (probably poplar), 83.2 × 51 cm, London, The National Gallery, bequeathed by Herbert Charles Coleman, 1949, inv. NG5930.

alt: Small round panel by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground, set in a square gilded surround on red velvet: Christ in half-length facing the viewer, with long light-brown hair, a short beard and a punched cross halo, wearing a blue-green tunic and a red mantle, raising his right hand in blessing and holding a closed green book in his left
caption: Christ Blessing, c. 1360, tempera and gold on panel, 18.7 × 18.1 cm, Brunswick (Maine), Bowdoin College Museum of Art, Gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation, inv. 1961.100.4.

alt: Three Gothic panels by Allegretto Nuzi on gold ground: in the centre the Crucifixion, with Christ on the Cross, two lamenting angels and a pelican in a nest on a tree at the top, the fainting Virgin in a dark mantle supported by holy women, Mary Magdalene in red kneeling at the foot of the Cross, Saint John in a pink mantle and soldiers with spears and a man in a turban on the right; on the left panel Saint Agnes in a pink-orange gown holding a lamb; on the right panel a female saint in a dark green gown and red mantle
caption: The Crucifixion between Saint Agnes and a Female Martyr, tempera and gold on panel. Central panel: Fribourg (Switzerland), Church of the Ursuline Nuns; lateral panels: recovered by the Carabinieri's cultural heritage unit. The three panels were recomposed and exhibited together in Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica ""Bruno Molajoli"," from 3 September to 16 October 2022..

alt: Gothic triptych on gold ground by Allegretto Nuzi. In the centre the Virgin, crowned and wearing a gold-patterned mantle, is enthroned with the Christ Child, surrounded by tiers of haloed angels and four standing saints, with an inscription on the base of the throne. In the left panel Saint Anthony Abbot, bearded and in a brown hooded habit, holds a tau-shaped staff and raises his right hand. In the right panel the young Saint Julian, in a gold brocade tunic and dark cloak, holds a lance with a red banner. The gables show the Crucified Christ in a quatrefoil between two half-length figures, the Angel Gabriel on the left and the Virgin Annunciate on the right
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Angels and Saints, between Saints Anthony Abbot and Julian, tempera and gold on panel, 1369, Macerata, Duomo di San Giuliano.

alt: Fresco by Allegretto Nuzi and workshop in a pointed lunette framed by a band of red, white and green geometric ornament. A dark boat sails across a grey-green sea between two ochre rocky shores. On the left, Saint Ursula's red-haired companions stand in a close row with hands joined in prayer; at the centre Ursula, haloed and in a pale gown with red dots, crosses her hands on her breast. On the right stand a cardinal in a red hat, Pope Cyriacus in a tall white tiara, and a bearded helmsman in red working the steering oar. A white sail and a white banner with a red cross rise above the passengers. Fragments of other scenes, an armoured leg and flames, are visible above the frame
caption: Allegretto Nuzi and Workshop, The Voyage of Saint Ursula and Pope Cyriacus, c. 1365, fresco, Fabriano, church of San Domenico (formerly Santa Lucia Novella), Chapel of Saint Ursula (also known as the Chapel of Saint Michael).

alt: Fresco lunette on a dark blue-black ground. A young woman with long loose reddish hair, wearing a pale off-the-shoulder gown with long hanging sleeves, sits on red patterned cushions on the back of a scaly grey-green dragon. She holds a long staff in her right hand and raises a golden chalice in her left, and one bare foot rests on stylised blue and white waves. The dragon's long tail curls behind her, and seven horned heads with open, fanged mouths rise on serpentine necks to the right, each labelled with a vice: SUPERBIA, INVIDIA, ACCIDIA, IRA, AVARITIA, GULA, LUXURIA. A Latin inscription at the top names the figure as Babylon the Great. The lunette is framed by red bands, with green and red foliage on the vault above
caption: Allegretto Nuzi (or Francescuccio Ghissi?), Babylon the Great Seated on the Seven-Headed Beast, mid-1360s, fresco, Fabriano, church of San Domenico (formerly Santa Lucia Novella), sacristy, probably the former chapter hall of the Dominican convent.

alt: Gothic cross vault decorated with fresco, seen from below. Four diagonal ribs painted with bands of red, blue and white quatrefoil and lozenge ornament meet at a small carved boss. In the lower web, best preserved, the young Saint John the Evangelist, haloed, in a green tunic and ochre mantle, sits on a pink Gothic throne with a pointed canopy, writing at a slanting desk and raising his right hand towards his head. The throne stands on a platform with an orange patterned carpet set against a blue-green ground. The other three webs are largely lost, showing only fragments of thrones, draperies and desks on blue. Circular medallions stand at the corners of the webs; one shows a winged ox, the others are faded or empty
caption: Allegretto Nuzi (attr.), The Four Evangelists, third quarter of the 14th century, fresco, Perugia, basilica of San Domenico, Cappella di San Nicolò (now Cappella del Nome di Gesù), vault.

alt: Fragmentary fresco of Saint John the Evangelist, shown from the knees up against a dark blue-black ground with extensive paint losses. The youthful, beardless saint has short curling auburn hair and a halo incised with radiating lines. He looks out at the viewer with a calm, slightly serious expression. He wears a pale tunic with a round neckline and long sleeves, and a red mantle falls from his left shoulder and wraps around his lower body in broad folds. With both hands he holds a closed book with a greenish cover against his chest. The upper part of the wall above the figure is covered by plain plaster
caption: Allegretto Nuzi (attr.), Saint John the Evangelist, traditionally dated 1336 (?), fresco, Fabriano, church of Santa Maria Maddalena (property of the Pia Università dei Cartai), right wall.

alt: Detached fresco, heavily damaged, mounted on canvas within a dark frame; large areas of loss are filled with neutral grey plaster. On the right, Christ sits on a green architectural throne, bearded, with long reddish-blond hair and a halo. He wears a pale greenish-blue tunic with a small rectangular gold ornament on the breast and a rose-red mantle draped over his shoulders and knees. His right hand is raised, open, towards the Virgin, and his left rests on his lap. On the left, the Virgin kneels in profile, haloed, wearing a dark mantle edged with gold over a red dress, her hands crossed on her breast and her face lifted towards Christ. Fragments of a painted frame survive along the left and lower edges
caption: The Virgin Interceding with Christ Enthroned, 1360-70, detached fresco transferred to canvas, 144 × 84 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli". It comes from the church of San Giovanni del Cantone in Fabriano, demolished in 1903.

alt: Gothic cusped panel painting, much abraded. The crowned Virgin sits frontally on a green stone throne with scrolled armrests, set on a low dais. She wears a red dress and a dark blue-black mantle patterned with gold vine leaves and bunches of grapes, edged with a gold border, and a dark veil over her head. On her left knee she holds the Christ Child, who turns and reaches up towards her; his pale garment is touched with blue. Behind her hangs a white cloth of honour decorated with blue trefoils and small red crosses. In the gable above, a roundel contains the half-length blessing Christ holding a book, surrounded by three red seraphim
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned, with the Blessing Christ and Seraphim, 1370, tempera and gold on a cusped panel, 182.9 × 68.3 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli", from the church of San Nicolò in Fabriano.

Head of the Christ Child (fragment of a Saint Christopher?), c. 1360, detached fresco mounted on a support, 52.7 × 29.4 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli", from the great vaulted passageway (voltone) of the Palazzo del Podestà in Fabriano.

alt: Four fragments of fresco arranged in a square grid within a wooden frame, each showing a haloed half-length figure inside a painted grey-white circular frame on a black ground. Top left: King David, crowned, with short curly brown hair and beard, holding a sceptre in his right hand and a closed book in his left, dressed in red and ochre. Top right: an elderly bearded prophet in profile wearing a white pointed cap, raising his right hand and holding an unrolled scroll with an inscription. Bottom left: a saint with long wavy white hair and a long beard, wrapped in an orange mantle, probably the apostle Andrew; part of this roundel is lost and filled with plain plaster. Bottom right: a saint with short grey hair and beard, raising his right hand in a gesture of speech and holding a scroll, probably the apostle Peter

alt: Detached fresco from a street shrine, displayed in a round-arched niche. On a blue ground, the crowned Virgin stands at the centre in a blue mantle scattered with gold stars over a red dress, holding the Christ Child on her right arm. The Child holds a scroll and turns towards Saint Catherine of Alexandria on the left, who wears a pale blue gown and extends her hand to receive the ring. On the right, a second haloed female saint in a golden gown raises her hand; below her, the kneeling donor, probably a knight, is almost entirely lost. Two winged angels hover above the Virgin. The vault of the niche is painted with dark red foliage and a lozenge at the top. In the right embrasure stands Saint Lucy; in the left, only the halo of another saint survives. The lower part of the fresco is heavily abraded.
caption: The Mystic Marriage of Saint Catherine of Alexandria, with a Female Saint Presenting a Kneeling Donor, 1360-70, detached fresco mounted on a support, 216.4 × 150.2 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli", from a street shrine (edicola) in Via San Filippo, Fabriano, detached in 1971.

alt: Medieval parchment manuscript page written in brown ink in two dense columns of small Gothic cursive script. In the upper half of the left column, a few lines of red text mark the heading of a new story, followed by a large red initial F decorated with fine blue pen flourishes. Smaller initials appear below it, one blue and one red. The pages are slightly stained and the inner edge of the binding is visible at the right.
caption: Giovanni Boccaccio, Decameron, autograph, c. 1370; Berlin, Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin – Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Ms. Ham. 90, fol. 84v (Day VIII, tale 3). Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Very wide medieval fresco in faded reds and ochres. At the left, an elegant hunting party on horseback halts before three open coffins containing corpses in increasing decay, while hermits occupy a rocky mountain above with a small chapel. At the centre, a rocky cleft divides the scene and a crowd of beggars gestures upward. In the sky at the right, angels and winged demons fight over small naked souls. At the lower right, richly dressed young men and women sit in a grove of orange trees with musicians, unaware of Death flying toward them with a scythe
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), The Triumph of Death, c. 1336–1341, fresco (detached), Camposanto Monumentale (south wall), Pisa.

alt: Large medieval fresco of the Last Judgement. At the top, Christ and the Virgin Mary sit side by side in two almond-shaped glories with rainbow borders, flanked by rows of seated apostles. Below, angels blow trumpets and hold scrolls, while armoured archangels with swords separate two dense crowds of resurrected figures: the blessed on the left, the condemned on the right. The painted surface is faded and shows the joins of the detached sections.
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Last Judgement, c. 1336–1341, fresco (detached), Camposanto Monumentale (south wall), Pisa.

alt: Large medieval fresco of Hell painted almost entirely in reds and browns. A gigantic horned Lucifer stands at the centre of a rocky mountain divided into tiers of cave-like compartments, devouring sinners while serpents issue from his body. Around him, demons torment crowds of naked souls with fire, cauldrons, and instruments of torture. At the upper right, a pocket of rock encloses a dense cluster of small souls; at the left edge appear haloed figures from the adjoining Last Judgement
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Hell, c. 1336–1341, fresco (detached, with later repainting), Camposanto Monumentale (south wall), Pisa.

alt: Very wide medieval fresco of a rocky desert landscape in pale ochres and greens, scattered with small chapels, huts, and caves. Dozens of elderly hermits in brown and grey habits pray, read, weave baskets, draw water, and converse across the terraced mountainside. A river with boats and a small bridge runs along the lower edge. Some hermits confront small dark demons and animals; large patches of plaster are lost, leaving blank areas
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Thebaid (Lives of the Desert Fathers), c. 1336–1341, fresco (detached), Camposanto Monumentale (south wall), Pisa.

alt: Triangular web of a Gothic vault frescoed in red-brown, framed by white ribs with red geometric borders. At the centre, a quatrefoil medallion with red and white ornamental bands encloses an elderly haloed prophet with a long ochre beard, dressed in pale robes, holding an unfurled scroll whose surface is abraded and blackened in patches
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr., after Ghiberti), Prophet holding a scroll, c. 1315, fresco, vault web of the former armarium (Cappella di San Jacopo), Badia a Settimo, Scandicci (Florence).

alt: Gothic vault web frescoed in mottled red-brown, framed by white ribs with red ornament. A quatrefoil medallion encloses a haloed bearded figure whose halo has turned black, draped in pale blue-grey robes, holding up a large unfurled scroll; the painted surface is severely abraded, with the design surviving mainly as ghostly outlines
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr., after Ghiberti), Prophet (or apostle) with unfurled scroll, c. 1315, fresco, vault web of the former armarium (Cappella di San Jacopo), Badia a Settimo, Scandicci (Florence).

alt: Triangular web of a Gothic vault in deep red-brown, bordered by white ribs with red star-and-chequer ornament meeting at a painted boss. A haloed figure in pale yellow-white robes sits frontally on a large architectural marble throne with a high back and projecting stepped footrest; the surface is heavily abraded, the face nearly effaced, the throne drawn in confident perspective lines.
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr., after Ghiberti), Enthroned evangelist, c. 1315, fresco, vault web of the former armarium (Cappella di San Jacopo), Badia a Settimo, Scandicci (Florence).

alt: Gothic vault web in mottled red-brown framed by white ribs with red ornament. A haloed, bearded evangelist in a dark red tunic and pale mantle sits frontally on a wide architectural throne, one hand raised before his chest; at his feet, between the folds of his robe, crouches a dark, heavily damaged four-legged winged creature, his evangelist symbol. The surface is abraded throughout
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr., after Ghiberti), Enthroned evangelist with his symbol, c. 1315, fresco, vault web of the former armarium (Cappella di San Jacopo), Badia a Settimo, Scandicci (Florence).

alt: Fragmentary medieval fresco under a stone arch. In the lunette above, a half-length Christ with open arms displays his wounds among the instruments of the Passion against dark blue. Below, the Virgin in a blue mantle sits on a golden throne with a patterned cloth of honour, holding the standing Christ Child whose face is lost; to the left stand a young saint and a sainted pope in a white tiara and red cope. Large areas of bare plaster interrupt the scene
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Christ in Pietà, with the Madonna and Child Enthroned and Saints, probably 1320s, fresco, Cathedral of Arezzo.

alt: Nearly square medieval painting of the Virgin and Child on a dark red ground framed by a red-and-black border of leaf motifs. The Virgin, in a very dark blue mantle over a bright red dress, sits on a pale green and ochre Gothic throne with pointed openings and pinnacle finials, turning her head toward the Child. The curly-haired Christ Child, in a red tunic patterned with small gold stars, sits on her lap holding her hand. The edges of the panel are worn and damaged.
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Virgin and Child Enthroned, first half of the 14th century, tempera on panel, 58 × 55 cm, Church of San Donato, Pergognano (Castiglion Fiorentino, Arezzo).

alt: Tall arched gold-ground panel in a gilded frame: Christ, in a red tunic and a blue mantle streaked with gold, holds a sceptre and crowns the Virgin seated beside him on a wide throne hung with a red and gold cloth; a blue starry arc and a dense choir of haloed angels with a vielle, lutes, a psaltery and a portative organ rise above them, other angels lean over the throne, and three small angels kneel at its foot between two dark cartouches bearing the date 1372 and the painters' names
caption: Donato and Catarino di Marco, Coronation of the Virgin, signed and dated August 1372, tempera and gold on panel, Venice, Fondazione Querini Stampalia, Pinacoteca. Central panel of a dismembered polyptych.

alt: Arched gold-ground panel: Christ, crowned and in a rose tunic and gold-patterned blue mantle, sets a crown on the head of the Virgin seated beside him on a shared throne; behind them hang an orange cloth with dark floral motifs and a starry blue hemisphere, over which eight angels lean, some playing a lute, a portative organ and a vielle; a three-line signature with the date 1375 runs along the step below
caption: Coronation of the Virgin, signed and dated March 1375, tempera and gold on panel, 89 × 58 cm, Venice, Gallerie dell'Accademia, cat. 16 (purchased from Count Vincenzo Galli, 1877).

alt: Three unframed gold-ground panels shown side by side. In the arched central panel Christ, in a blue tunic and red mantle, crowns the Virgin, who wears a blue mantle with large gold motifs; they sit on a pink Gothic throne before a starry blue arc with five angels above, and a fragmentary signature runs along the base. At the left stands Saint Lucy, crowned, in red and green, holding a lamp; at the right Saint Nicholas of Tolentino, in a black habit, holds a red book
caption: Coronation of the Virgin with Saints Lucy and Nicholas of Tolentino, signed, after 1375, tempera and gold on panel, Venice, Gallerie dell'Accademia, cat. 702 (purchased from Tommaso Mazzoli of Venice, 1902).

alt: Gilded Gothic polyptych in three tiers. In the centre the Virgin, in a blue mantle with large gold motifs, sits on a flowering meadow holding the Child, with a tiny donor kneeling at her side. Four standing saints flank her: Anthony Abbot, John the Baptist, Christopher carrying the Christ Child through water, and James the Great. Above are four half-length saints and, at the top, a Crucifixion between two small standing female saints. A painted base carries the signature
caption: Madonna and Child, the Crucifixion, and Saints, signed, c. 1380–1389, tempera and gold on panel, 176.5 × 185.9 cm with frame and original base, Baltimore, The Walters Art Museum, inv. 37.635 (acquired by Henry Walters, 1908–1909).

alt: Small gold-ground panel in a gilded frame with a cusped arch and twisted colonnettes. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle with fine gold scrollwork over a red dress, sits low on a flowering meadow and nurses the Child, who is wrapped in an orange and gold cloth. Gold rays spread from her figure, a white crescent moon lies at her feet, and a small scroll at the lower right carries the painter's signature
caption: Madonna of Humility, signed, 1380–82, tempera and gold on panel, 40.6 × 33.4 cm, Worcester, Massachusetts, Worcester Art Museum, inv. 1923.213 (from Eugene Bolton, London).

alt: The Virgin, in a plain blue mantle over a red dress, bends her head towards the Child, who lies across her arm wrapped in an orange cloth and turns to look up at her. Both have gold haloes, and thin gold rays spread from them across a bright red ground with a lobed upper edge. Grey patches mark losses in the haloes and at the Virgin's breast
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.) or a follower, Madonna of Humility, 1370–80, tempera on panel, 85 × 67 cm, Faenza, Pinacoteca Comunale, inv. 102.

alt: Gold-ground panel under a round gilded arch with carved foliage in the corners. The Virgin, in a blue mantle with large gold motifs and a green lining over a pink dress, sits low on a broad red ground and nurses the Child, who wears a red tunic patterned in gold. A small gold sun with rays shines on her breast and a gold star on her shoulder, faint gold rays spread around her, and a Latin inscription naming the Madonna of Humility runs along the bottom
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.), Madonna of Humility, late 1370s, tempera and gold on panel, 79.6 × 54.6 cm (91.5 × 70 × 4 cm framed), Cleveland, The Cleveland Museum of Art, inv. 1963.500, gift of Dr. Rudolf J. Heinemann.

alt: Small round-arched gold-ground panel. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle scattered with small flower sprigs over a pink dress, sits low and nurses the Child, who is wrapped in an orange and yellow cloth on her green-lined lap. An orange cushion lies at her side, and a dark flowering meadow fills the lower right corner
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.), Madonna of Humility, tempera and gold on panel, 28.9 × 25.4 cm, Columbus, Ohio, Columbus Museum of Art, inv. 1931.041, gift of Ferdinand Howald.

alt: Unframed gold-ground panel. Christ, in a red tunic and a dark mantle patterned with large gold star-shaped motifs, holds a long sceptre and places a jewelled crown on the head of the Virgin, who sits beside him with joined hands in a matching dark mantle. Behind them hangs a red cloth patterned in gold, held up by winged angels, and above it a dark blue sky full of gold stars shows a sun with a face at the left and a crescent moon at the right, under a crowded choir of haloed angels
caption: Coronation of the Virgin, fourteenth century, tempera and gold on poplar panel, 120 × 75 cm, St Petersburg, State Hermitage Museum, inv. ГЭ-6662 (formerly N. P. Likhachev collection; State Russian Museum from 1914; Hermitage from 1923).

alt: Small cusped-arched panel set in a later gilded frame on green velvet. Christ, in a red tunic patterned with gold and a dark blue mantle, raises a jewelled crown over the head of the Virgin, who sits at the left with joined hands in a blue mantle with gold flowers and a white veil. They sit in a dark architectural throne with small angel heads looking in from the sides, and above a cornice three winged angels lean over a parapet
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.), Coronation of the Virgin, 1370s, tempera and gold on panel, 27.8 × 13.7 cm, Munich, Lingenauber collection.

alt: Large shaped wooden cross with a gold ground and stepped edges. The dead Christ hangs on a dark painted cross, his head fallen to his right shoulder, his ribs and swollen belly sharply modelled, a thin white loincloth at his hips and his feet crossed. In the quatrefoil terminals the grieving Virgin in green appears at the left, Saint John in pink and blue at the right, and a winged archangel holding a staff and an orb at the top. A small titulus above the head reads I.N.R.I., and the lower terminal shows a dark rocky mound
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.), Painted Crucifix, 1375–1400, tempera and gold on panel, 348 × 250 cm, Zadar, collection of sacred art.

alt: Saint Dominic Altarpiece
caption: Saint Dominic Altarpiece, 1344-45, tempera and gold on panel, Central panel: 175 × 74 cm; each wing: 163 × 93 cm (ensemble: 175 × 260 cm), Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, Pisa.

alt: Madonna and Child with Saint Anne
caption: Madonna and Child with Saint Anne, 1340-45, tempera on panel, 84.9 × 56 cm (frame 101.3 × 76.5 × 14.6 cm), Princeton University Art Museum, Princeton.

caption: The Virgin and Child, c. 1345, tempera and gold on panel, 48 x 42 cm, Museo Nacional del Prado, Madrid.

alt: The Virgin and Child
caption: The Virgin and Child, c. 1325, tempera and gold on panel, 63.5 x 51.5 x 3 cm (with microclimate frame: 66.8 x 60.5 cm), Louvre Abu Dhabi.

alt: Small gilded tabernacle panel with a pointed Gothic frame and twisted colonnettes: the Virgin, seated low in a dark blue gold-patterned mantle and red gown, nurses the Christ Child against a gold ground.
caption: Our Lady of Humility, c. 1365, tempera and gold on panel, 34.6 × 19.9 cm, Pinacoteca Vaticana, Vatican City.

alt: Two-register panel on gold: above, the Man of Sorrows in his tomb between two mourning angels; below, the Christ Child lying on the ground, adored by two angels, the Virgin and St Joseph.
caption: Dead Christ and angels; Adoration of Baby Jesus, c. 1360, tempera and gold on panel, 39.3 × 28.5 cm, Pinacoteca Vaticana, Vatican City.

alt: The Virgin of Humility seated on the ground nursing the Child, in a dark blue mantle with gold lozenges and a red gown with gold birds, before a white cloth of honour tied with red ribbons; a crescent moon lies at her feet.
caption: Our Lady of Humility, 1359, tempera on panel, 173 × 122 cm, Pinacoteca civica Bruno Molajoli, Fabriano.

alt: Five-part gabled polyptych: the Virgin and Child at the centre, a bishop saint and St John the Evangelist on the left, St John the Baptist and a young martyr on the right, small figures in the gables; the gold is heavily abraded.
caption: Madonna and Child between a Saint Bishop and Saints John the Evangelist, John the Baptist and Venantius; in the cusps: Christ adored by two angels between Saint Catherine of Alexandria and Saint Anthony the Abbot, 1370, tempera on panel, 122 × 173 cm, Pinacoteca civica Bruno Molajoli, Fabriano.

alt: The Virgin of Humility nursing the Child against a gold ground tooled with vine scrolls and scattered dark stars, in a dark mantle with vine leaves and a red gown patterned with birds.
caption: Our Lady of Humility, tempera and gold on panel, 95 × 77 cm, Pinacoteca civica, Fermo.

alt: The Virgin and Child enthroned cheek to cheek, in a dark blue mantle with gold lozenges before a red and gold cloth of honour, with three angels on each side, hands joined or crossed.
caption: Enthroned Madonna with Six Angels, tempera and gold on panel, 138 × 99 cm, Musée du Petit Palais, Avignon.

alt: Small hinged triptych in a glazed case on green velvet: the nursing Virgin of Humility in the centre, the Nativity in the left wing and the Crucifixion in the right, the Annunciation in the two gables.
caption: Our Lady of Humility; The Nativity; The Crucifixion; The Annunciation (top left and right), tempera on panel, 450 × 209 mm (central panel), National Trust, Polesden Lacey, Surrey.

alt: St John, at left, raises his hand toward a bier draped in red and carried by two bearers, while a kneeling man entreats him and a woman raises her arms before a white building with a tower; a red seraph hovers at upper left; the frame nameplate reads Allegretto Nuzi.
caption: The Resurrection of Drusiana, c. 1370, tempera on panel, 34.3 × 36.8 cm, Portland Art Museum, Portland.

alt: Church of the Resurrection of Christ in Veroia
caption: Church of the Resurrection of Christ in Veroia, Greece.

caption: Virgin and Child (Hodegetria), 1315, tempera on wood panel (portable icon), Byzantine Museum, Veroia, Greece.

alt: The Crucifixion
caption: The Crucifixion, 1315, fresco, church of the Resurrection of Christ, Veroia, Greece.

alt: The Resurrection of Christ
caption: The Resurrection of Christ, 1315, fresco, church of the Resurrection of Christ, Veroia, Greece.

alt: The Dormition of the Virgin
caption: The Dormition of the Virgin, 1315, fresco, church of the Resurrection of Christ, Veroia, Greece.

alt: Annunciation, Apse, and Saints
caption: Annunciation, Apse, and Saints, 1315, fresco, church of the Resurrection of Christ, Veroia, Greece.

alt: Four great Church Fathers
caption: Four great Church Fathers: John Chrysostom, Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, and in the fourth position probably Athanasius the Great, 1315, fresco, church of the Resurrection of Christ, Veroia, Greece.

caption: Church of St. Nicholas Orphanos, Thessaloniki, Greece.

alt: Frescoes in the Church of St. Nicholas Orphanos, Thessaloniki
caption: Two Deaths, One Wall: Kalliergis and the Theology of Sacred Passage, 1310-20, fresco, church of St. Nicholas Orphanos, Thessaloniki, Greece.

alt: Painted crucifix by Giovanni da Rimini in San Francesco, Mercatello sul Metauro: the dead Christ against a gold patterned cloth of honour, with a dark crossbeam, a blue lower shaft and a blue footrest, and polylobed gold terminals showing the mourning Virgin in a dark mantle, Saint John the Evangelist in a rose mantle, and the blessing Redeemer above a red tablet.
caption: Painted crucifix, signed and dated 1309 (or 1314), tempera and gold on panel, 300 × 227 cm, church of San Francesco, Mercatello sul Metauro.

alt: Diotallevi Crucifix by Giovanni da Rimini, Museo della Città, Rimini: the dead Christ with a transparent loincloth on a dark cross with gilded lobed terminals showing the mourning Virgin, Saint John the Evangelist and the blessing Redeemer with the Gospel book
caption: Diotallevi crucifix, 1300–05, tempera and gold on panel, 185 × 179 cm, Rimini, Museo della Città "Luigi Tonini", inv. 11 PQ.

alt: Painted crucifix attributed to Giovanni da Rimini in San Lorenzo, Talamello: the dead Christ on a dark blue cross with rectangular stepped terminals showing the mourning Virgin, Saint John the Evangelist, the blessing Redeemer above, and the skull of Adam at the foot
caption: Giovanni da Rimini (attr.), Painted crucifix, 1300–05 or after 1309 (dating disputed), tempera and gold on panel, 230 × 160 cm, church of San Lorenzo, Talamello.

alt: Painted crucifix by Giovanni da Rimini, known as the Goudstikker Crucifix. The panel is cut down to the shape of the cross itself: the dead Christ hangs against a dark green cross edged in gold, his head fallen to the right, eyes closed, with a gold cruciform halo decorated with red panels. A transparent white loincloth reveals the legs beneath. At the top, a red tablet bears the Greek christogram IC XC in white letters. Blood falls in thin trickles from the hands, side and feet. Moretti Gallery, London
caption: Painted crucifix ("Goudstikker Crucifix"), 1309–14, tempera and gold on panel, 160.5 × 130 cm, London, Moretti Gallery (formerly Jacques Goudstikker collection, Amsterdam).

alt: Gilded panel by Giovanni da Rimini divided by red ornamental bands into six scenes from the life of Christ: top row, the Nativity with the bath of the Child and the Crucifixion; middle row, the Lamentation over Christ's body on a pink tomb and the Descent into Limbo, with Christ raising Adam from a dark cave; bottom row, a winged angel on the tomb before the three Holy Women with the Risen Christ behind, and the Last Judgement with Christ enthroned in a blue mandorla above the rising dead. Gallerie Nazionali di Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini, Rome
caption: Scenes from the Life of Christ (Nativity, Crucifixion, Lamentation, Descent into Limbo, Resurrection, Last Judgement), 1300–05, tempera and gold on panel, 52.5 × 34.5 cm, Rome, Gallerie Nazionali di Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini, inv. 1441. Photo: Francesco Bini (Sailko), Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

alt: Gilded panel by Giovanni da Rimini with four scenes of unequal size. Upper left: mourners bow at an altar-tomb beneath a hexagonal canopy while, high above, Saint John the Evangelist is received in heaven by Christ, the Virgin, angels and saints. Upper right: Christ crowns the Virgin on a Gothic throne above a crowd of angels looking up. Lower left: Saint Catherine, crowned, preaches from a pulpit to philosophers and the enthroned Emperor Maxentius. Lower right: Saint Francis kneels in a rocky landscape receiving the stigmata from a red seraph, beside Saint John the Baptist. National Gallery, London
caption: Scenes from the Lives of the Virgin and other Saints, probably about 1300–05, egg tempera on wood, 54.4 × 36.5 cm, London, National Gallery, NG6656. Acquired with a generous donation from Ronald S. Lauder, 2015. Photo © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Small gilded panel by Giovanni da Rimini in two registers. Above, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle bends her head to press her cheek against the Child, who twists toward her with his back to the viewer; two angels in white with dark wings hold a purple cloth behind them. Below, five saints stand in a row against the gold: Francis in a brown habit, the Archangel Michael with wings and a globe, a bishop saint with mitre and crozier, the crowned Catherine in red, and Clare in a black veil. Pinacoteca Comunale, Faenza.
caption: Virgin and Child with Two Angels and Saints Francis, Michael the Archangel, Augustine (?), Catherine of Alexandria and Clare, 1300–05, tempera and gold on panel, 50 × 35 cm, Faenza, Pinacoteca Comunale, inv. 92.

alt: Damaged fresco of the Dormition of the Virgin by Giovanni da Rimini in the church of Sant'Agostino, Rimini. At the centre Christ, in a red mantle, stands behind the deathbed holding the Virgin's soul as a small figure wrapped in white. Crowds of haloed apostles and young figures surround him in overlapping rows. The Virgin lies on a long dark bier, her pale face visible at the right end. The dark background has lost most of its blue paint, large patches of plaster are missing, and painted twisted columns frame the scene at both sides
caption: Dormition of the Virgin, before 1307 (possibly before 1303), fresco, Rimini, church of Sant'Agostino (formerly San Giovanni Evangelista), chapel at the base of the campanile. Photo: Sailko, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0.

alt: Hexagonal baptismal font in the Pieve di Santa Maria, Arezzo, on a stepped stone base: three white marble relief panels attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1332, set into its faces — the Baptism of Christ at the centre between the young John led into the desert and the Ecce Agnus Dei — beneath a plain moulded cornice.
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), Baptismal font with three Stories of St John the Baptist (John led into the desert, Ecce Agnus Dei, Baptism of Christ), marble reliefs in a hexagonal stone chest, c. 1332, Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1332, on the baptismal font of the Pieve di Santa Maria, Arezzo: an angel flies horizontally across the top, drapery streaming over the frame's edge, arms extended toward a grove of trees on a smooth rocky hill, while below the young Baptist in his tufted camel-hair tunic climbs with hands joined in prayer, face upturned to the messenger
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), The young Baptist sent into the desert by an angel, marble relief panel of the baptismal font, c. 1332, Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1332, on the baptismal font of the Pieve di Santa Maria, Arezzo: the Baptist in his camel-hair tunic stands at left among trees, arm extended toward a pressed crowd of seven figures at right, within which the haloed Christ gazes frontally at the viewer between two haloed companions
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), The Baptist points out Christ (Ecce Agnus Dei), marble relief panel of the baptismal font, c. 1332, Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1332, on the baptismal font of the Pieve di Santa Maria, Arezzo: Christ stands waist-deep in the smooth mound of the Jordan, a carved drop of water running down his chest, while the Baptist lays a hand flat on his head from the left bank and three bowing angels hold his garments at either side.
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), The Baptism of Christ, marble relief panel of the baptismal font, c. 1332, Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Marble relief of the Madonna and Child enthroned between two standing angels beneath a carved canopy, signed by Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1330–1340, vestibule of the upper Oratory of San Bernardino, Siena. The sculptor's Latin signature runs along the lower frame
caption: Madonna and Child enthroned between two angels, signed ("Ioh(anne)s magist(r)i Agostini de Se(n)is me fecit"), 1330–40, marble, Siena, vestibule of the upper Oratory of San Bernardino (Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra).

alt: Chapel of Ciuto Tarlati in Arezzo Cathedral: Gothic marble aedicule by Giovanni di Agostino, 1334, with Annunciation statuettes and gable relief, framing the Crucifixion fresco attributed to the Maestro del Vescovado with a kneeling armoured donor, above a reused fourth-century sarcophagus
caption: Arezzo, Cathedral of Santi Pietro e Donato, fifth bay of the right aisle: chapel of Ciuto Tarlati. Marble aedicule and sculptures (Annunciation, gable relief) contracted with Giovanni di Agostino on 28 January 1334; Crucifixion and archivolt frescoes attributed to the Maestro del Vescovado, c. 1334 or shortly after; below, a reused fourth-century strigilated sarcophagus.

alt: Marble Sacrament tabernacle attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331–32: the archangel Gabriel and the Virgin Annunciate flank a central door opening beneath crocketed Gothic gables; from Sant'Eugenio a Monistero, now in the chapel of Palazzo Chigi Saracini, Siena

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, from a dismembered saint's shrine in Volterra: an elderly bearded saint at left hands a garment down to a bowing pauper, while five more poor men with staffs, sacks and wrapped heads press forward to receive; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, from a dismembered saint's shrine in Volterra: a procession of tonsured religious carries the bearded corpse of the saint shoulder-high toward the arched portal of a crenellated church at right, accompanied by a mitred bishop and a young acolyte at left; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra.
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), The translation of the saint's body, relief from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Fragmentary marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331: a winged angel with a soft oval face and downcast eyes, mantle bordered by an embroidered hem, raises one hand high and lowers the other over the surviving folds of a curtain whose swags hang from the top edge; the slab is broken diagonally where the curtain and the saint's effigy once continued; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra.
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Curtain-bearing angel, fragment from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Fragmentary marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331: a winged angel in profile leans left with its whole body, one raised hand gripping the gathered knot of a great curtain whose swags fill the upper corner, the other hand lowered to press the cloth against its hip; from a dismembered saint's shrine, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Curtain-drawing angel, fragment from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Marble effigy of a dead saint attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, from a dismembered shrine in Volterra: an elderly bearded man in a hooded religious habit lies full length, hands crossed at the wrists on his body, head tilted slightly outward, the drapery running in long parallel folds to the feet; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra

alt: Polychrome wooden statue of the crucified Christ without its cross, arms raised diagonally. The emaciated body shows carved ribs, a bleeding side wound with painted blood running down the right leg, and red scourge marks on the limbs. The bowed head with closed eyes and brown hair is serene; a long grey-green loincloth with gilded borders reaches the knees
caption: Christ Crucified, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, height 210.2 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Life-size wooden statue of the dead Christ lying on his back, seen foreshortened from the feet, whose soles show carved nail holes. The forearms are crossed over the lower chest, the bearded head rests with closed eyes, and a deeply folded cloth wraps the hips. The painted surface is almost entirely worn away, exposing bare brown wood
caption: Dead Christ, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, length 188 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Polychrome wooden Pietà: the Virgin, seated in a dark hooded mantle with a pale, still face, holds the rigid pale body of the dead Christ horizontally across her lap. His bearded head falls sharply backward over her knee with mouth open, one arm dangling, and a long white cloth in sharp parallel folds wraps his hips and thighs. Red wounds mark the chest and limbs
caption: Pietà, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, height 131.8 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Polychrome wooden statue of a young, beardless St John the Evangelist standing with hands tightly clasped at his chest. His head tilts toward one shoulder, brows knotted and eyes raised in grief. He wears a grey-brown tunic with a gilded collar under a deep green, gold-bordered mantle that crosses the body in heavy diagonal folds, falling to his feet on a small octagonal base
caption: St John the Evangelist, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, height 171.6 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Polychrome wooden statue of the grieving Virgin standing upright, entirely wrapped in a dark hooded mantle falling to the ground. A white veil with ornamented ends frames her pale, still face with lowered eyes, and descends over a dark violet dress carved in dense vertical pleats. Her bare hands hang open and empty at her sides in a gesture of helpless sorrow
caption: Grieving Virgin, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, height 178.5 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Life-size wooden effigy of the dead Virgin lying on her back, seen foreshortened from the feet. Her forearms are crossed over the breast, one hand laid over the other arm, her pale aged face rests with closed eyes, framed by carved waves of hair. The dress covering the whole body is carved into long, thin parallel pleats that break over the feet in sharp angular folds. The painted surface is largely worn away to bare brown wood
caption: Dead Virgin, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, length 187 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Fourteenth-century painted wooden statue of an elderly, bareheaded Magus kneeling in profile, bowed deeply forward with hands folded on his chest; his red mantle is decorated with gilded floral patterns. Maestro dei Magi di Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica Bruno Molajoli, Fabriano.

Maestro dei Magi di Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica Bruno Molajoli, Fabriano.

alt: Fourteenth-century life-size painted wooden statue of a standing woman, presented in 2014 as St Helena though no surviving sign confirms it, with braided hair coiled about her head and no crown, in a fitted green bodice with applied bosses and a patterned skirt and mantle; a dark stump of the lost attribute survives between the fingers of her left hand at the hip. alt: Left panel of the Sterbini Diptych: on a gold ground, the half-length Virgin in a dark blue star-studded mantle holds the Christ Child, who reaches for a small bird offered by the grey-bearded Saint Joseph; below, three standing saints — Lawrence in a red patterned dalmatic, Philip in a pink mantle, and John the Baptist in a green mantle holding a scroll; Right panel of the Sterbini Diptych: above, Christ crucified against a gold sky with a flying angel, the Virgin in blue on the left, Saint John the Evangelist in a pink mantle on the right, and Mary Magdalene in red kneeling at the foot of the cross before a green wall; below, Saint Francis kneels in a rocky landscape receiving the stigmata from a red six-winged seraph, beside Saint Louis of Toulouse in a mitre and a blue cope sown with gold fleurs-de-lis.
caption: Sterbini Diptych, left panel: Virgin and Child with Saint Joseph; Saints Lawrence, Philip and John the Baptist; right panel: Crucifixion; Stigmatisation of Saint Francis; Saint Louis of Toulouse, third–fourth decade of the 14th century, tempera and gold on panel, 32.5 × 25.5 cm (each), Rome, Museo Nazionale del Palazzo di Venezia, inv. 10202.
