caption: Master of Campodonico (attr.), Last Judgement, Flagellation of Christ and Saints, 1320–1340, tempera on panel, 93 × 106 cm, La Valletta, MUŻA (già National Museum of Fine Arts).

alt: Gold-ground altarpiece. At the centre the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle with gold stars over a red dress, sits on a tall throne holding the Christ Child, with two winged archangels behind her. Six standing saints in two tiers flank each side, each named on a red band below. A small woman in black kneels at the Virgin's feet
caption: Virgin and Child Enthroned with Archangels, Saints and the Donor Elena (Dossal of Domina Elena), dated 1308, tempera and gold on panel, Cesi (Terni), church of Santa Maria Assunta, chapel of the Santissimo Sacramento (Archdiocese of Spoleto-Norcia).

alt: Gold-ground triptych with a tall central panel between two narrow wings. In the centre, inside a pointed mandorla edged in red and pale blue and lifted by eight winged angels, Christ embraces the Virgin, who leans her head against his; below, the apostles crowd behind a long pink marble tomb. Each wing holds four small scenes stacked one above another and separated by red inscription bands. On the left the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, receives a heavenly messenger, an angel, the apostle John and the gathered apostles. On the right the apostles surround her deathbed, carry her bier in procession and lower her body into the tomb
caption: Triptych of the Assumption and Dormition of the Virgin (the "Stella triptych"), c. 1300, tempera and gold on panel; central panel 186 × 92 cm (91 cm in AGORHA), each wing 177 × 44 cm. Paris, Musée Marmottan Monet, on deposit since 1993 from the Académie des Beaux-Arts, Institut de France (Ephrussi de Rothschild bequest). From the convent of Santi Stefano e Tommaso, called "della Stella", Spoleto.

alt: Large painted cross on a black background. Christ hangs with outstretched arms against a gold field, his head upright and his eyes open, his pale body wrapped in a striped loincloth. Two small angels with blue wings hover beneath his arms. The Virgin, in a dark mantle, stands to the left of his body and John, in pink, to the right. In the square ends of the arms stand two small saints, and at the top Christ blesses from a red mandorla between two angels. At his feet kneel Francis in a brown habit and Dominic in black and white, and blood runs down the shaft below
caption: Christus triumphans (painted cross with Christ blessing, the Virgin, John the Evangelist, Saints Stephen and Thomas, and Saints Francis and Dominic), c. 1300–1310, tempera and gold on panel, 245 × 158 cm. Spoleto, Museo Nazionale del Ducato di Spoleto, Rocca Albornoziana; probably from the convent of Santi Stefano e Tommaso, called "della Stella", Spoleto.

alt: Small open triptych with arched wings, its gold ground worn and darkened. In the upper half of the central panel, under a round arch divided by a red column, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle holds the Christ Child in red, and beside her Saint Anne in a grey mantle holds the child Mary; two small angels fly above. Below, Christ hangs on the cross between the Virgin and John, and to the right Christ kneels in prayer on a pale rocky hill with dark trees. Each wing holds three registers of standing saints in pairs, among them a bishop in a mitre, a friar in a brown habit, an angel and a figure in a black habit
caption: Attributed to the Maestro di Cesi, Portable triptych with the Virgin and Child and Saint Anne with the Child Mary Enthroned, the Crucifixion, the Agony in the Garden, and Saints including Augustine and Sperandeo, c. 1290–1325, tempera and gold on panel, c. 95 × 93 cm (open). Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria.

alt: Tall arched gold-ground panel. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle with a gold-studded border over a red dress, and a white veil striped with red, sits on a throne with round red cushions, her feet on a pale step above a blue-green floor. On her knee sits the Christ Child in an olive-green tunic and mantle, with a gilded cross halo; he reaches up to touch her face and holds a small scroll. In the corners above the arch, two half-length prophets hold scrolls that curve along the frame. A two-line inscription runs along the base
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (identified by recent scholarship with the late Maestro di Cesi), Madonna and Child Enthroned with a Donor and Two Prophets (Madonna della Selvetta), 1332, tempera and gold on panel, 157 × 63 cm. alt: Detached fresco: the Virgin, enthroned beneath a painted canopy with a pointed arch, nurses the Christ Child; two angels hold a patterned cloth of honour behind her. To the left stands Saint Lucy, her face lost to damage; to the right, Saint Catherine of Alexandria in a pleated gown and a mitred bishop saint with crozier raised in blessing. Painted balconies with geometric marble inlay recede on either side; areas of bare plaster mark old losses.
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned (Madonna lactans) with Saints Lucy, Catherine of Alexandria and Emilian (identified from the abbey's dedication), second decade of the 14th century, detached fresco transferred to a stretcher support, 349 × 346 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli", from the abbey of Sant'Emiliano in Congiuntoli, Scheggia e Pascelupo.

alt: Gothic chapel wall in fresco: a pointed lancet window with blue leaded glass is framed by painted marble ornament and four standing saints on two levels, several damaged. In the lunette above, a dead monk lies on a bed mourned by black-robed friars, while a mitred bishop amid four angels carries the small figure of his soul heavenward
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, Gothic chapel of Saint Augustine: window wall with flanking saints and, in the lunette, the Transitus of a Monk (the Hugues de Fontenay legend), first decades of the 14th century.

alt: View up into a quadripartite vault: four ribs painted with bands of chevrons, chequers and rosettes meet at a central boss. In the dark blue-grey webs, roundels contain half-length saints — a figure in a red mantle, a mitred bishop with a book, and another bishop holding an open scroll — with large areas of plaster loss
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, Gothic chapel: rib vault with half-length saints in medallions, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Detail of a fourteenth-century fresco: Christ, with cruciform halo and a red nail-wound on his extended right hand, draws aside his mantle at the breast while a youthful figure with long auburn hair reaches to touch the wound. Behind press haloed apostles, including grey-haired Peter, before rose-coloured architecture.
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, Magdalen chapel: the Risen Christ shows his wounds (probably the Incredulity of Thomas), detail, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Fourteenth-century fresco on a dark blue ground: at left a haloed bishop saint rides a white horse, right hand raised in blessing, attended by three angels, two holding lilies and one flying above. At right a tall pink prison tower with a wooden gallery; a man in a pale tunic climbs down from an opening, stepping on a crouching companion, while another figure holds up broken fetters toward the saint. Large plaster losses interrupt the lower centre.
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, chapel of Saint Augustine: Saint Augustine frees the prisoner from the tower, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Close view of a fourteenth-century fresco Crucifixion: the head and torso of Christ on an ochre cross against a dark slate-blue ground. His head, in a radiate halo with red jewelled compartments, sinks to the right shoulder with closed eyes; thin rivulets of dark red blood run from the side wound down his flank; a transparent loincloth veils the hips. The pale surface is worn and scratched
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, chapel of Saint Augustine: Crucifixion, detail of Christ, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Detail of a fourteenth-century fresco: four women in profile look up toward the left, praying. The first wears a gold fleur-de-lis crown and a white gown with jewelled bands; behind her stand a young woman in rose, an older woman in ochre, and an aged woman in grey-green with a deeply wrinkled face. At the left edge, red drapery and a pole with a knotted white cloth mark the object of their gaze, outside the frame.
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, Magdalen chapel: female devotees led by a crowned princess (probably the audience of the Magdalen's preaching at Marseille), detail, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Fourteenth-century fresco lunette: a mitred bishop saint, enthroned frontally in a red cope over white robes, extends both arms to place his hands on the heads of two kneeling young figures in courtly dress, each holding a small white object. Two differently patterned cloths of honour hang behind; small dark winged creatures — the expelled demons — fly toward the upper corners. A painted corbel cornice runs below; ornamental borders frame the arch.
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, chapel of Saint Augustine: Saint Augustine liberates two possessed, lunette, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Fresco of the Crucifixion filling a pointed lunette beneath a ribbed vault. Christ hangs on a tall cross inscribed INRI, flanked by six grieving angels whose bodies trail into clouds. On the left, the holy women support the fainting Virgin beside a small barred window cut into the wall; soldiers with spears, a sponge on a reed and a red banner crowd behind a rider on a brown horse. Mary Magdalene in green embraces the foot of the cross, beside a small kneeling donor in black. On the right, a rider on a white horse and helmeted soldiers look up at Christ, one raising his hand, while Saint John sits mourning in the lower corner. Ornamental bands and Evangelist symbols decorate the vault above
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Crucifixion, 1333. Fresco, altar wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto.
entry: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco

alt: View up into a ribbed cross vault painted in fresco. Four triangular compartments with deep blue grounds each hold a winged, haloed Evangelist with a human body and a book, their heads turned towards the central boss. The figure in the lowest compartment has the head of an eagle, identifying Saint John; the one on the right has a lion's head, the one on the left a human face, and the one at the top, seen upside down, cannot be read with certainty. The ribs carry bands of small geometric motifs in red and white, and broad borders of scrolling foliage and rosettes on a dark ground frame each compartment. At the bottom edge, the top of the Crucifixion with its INRI titulus and two angels is visible; on the left, rows of haloed figures from a side wall; on the right, part of an arched opening
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Vault with the Four Evangelists, 1333. Fresco, vault of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto.
entry: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco

alt: Fresco within a pointed arch showing the Virgin enthroned, wearing a white veil over her head and shoulders and a dark mantle over a red dress. The Christ Child, in a pale tunic and barefoot, stands on her lap, embracing her neck and pressing his cheek to hers. Behind them hangs a cloth of honour with a small red and white chequered pattern. At either side stands a haloed, winged angel in a brown mantle, hands held to the chest. The arch is framed by a band of scrolling foliage with white and orange flowers on a dark ground and an outer border with geometric inlay, resting on a painted corbel with sawtooth ornament
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Maestà between Two Angels, 1333. Fresco, upper part of the painted tabernacle, side wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto.

alt: Fresco of a tall standing Virgin in a white veil and grey-green mantle over a red dress, her head bowed towards the right. She draws her mantle open, and from beneath it the barefoot Christ Child, in a green tunic and cruciform halo, steps forward and reaches out his hand. On the right a smaller haloed nun in a brown habit and white veil kneels and raises both hands towards him. Behind the Virgin hangs a cloth patterned with white and red rosettes; to the right is a dark blue ground scattered with stars. An inscription at lower right reads SCA CLARA, and a border of red and white triangles runs along the arch at the edge
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), The Virgin Brings the Christ Child to the Blessed Chiara (traditionally La Madonna fa giocare Santa Chiara con Gesù Bambino), 1333. Fresco, narrative scene in the painted tabernacle, side wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto.

alt: Fresco on a dark blue-black ground. On the right, Christ, haloed, with long fair hair and beard and a sorrowful face, wears a long reddish-brown garment and steps forward with bent knee. He carries a wooden cross on his shoulder, its crossbar and titulus rising behind him, and grips the long shaft with both hands, driving its foot diagonally into the breast of a nun on the left. She stands facing him in a dark habit and white veil, with a golden halo, and lifts her hand beneath the foot of the cross. Christ stands on an ochre mound of ground. The surface is worn, with losses and whitish efflorescence, and part of another figure is visible at the right edge
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Christ Planting the Cross in the Heart of the Blessed Chiara (Cristo pianta la croce nel cuore di Chiara), 1333. Fresco, lower part of the painted tabernacle, side wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). alt: Fresco of a haloed nun in a black habit and white veil sitting upright on a bed, hands folded on her lap, eyes raised to heaven. Behind her a wall of square panels alternates dark red and ochre beneath a painted cornice with Gothic leaf ornament. Crowds of grieving nuns in white veils fill both sides, hands clasped. Two tonsured friars stand beside her: one raises his hand and holds a red book; the other rests his cheek on his hand and holds a small round flask. In the foreground a nun kneels at the bed looking up at her, and another, seen from behind in a dark mantle, kneels at the right. The bed is covered with an ochre cloth patterned in red
caption: Second hand of the chapel (Maestro di Sant'Alò?), Death of the Blessed Chiara, 1333. Not by the Primo Maestro: shown for comparison. Fresco, side wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto.

alt: Long, low painted altar panel on a gold ground with a jagged profile of gables and a raised central arch. At the centre, Christ hangs on the cross between angels, with the mystic pelican in a roundel above; below, the swooning Virgin among the holy women, Saint John, and soldiers with a red banner and a white horse. On either side, two registers of small scenes are separated by painted columns. On the left, the story of Saint Catherine of Alexandria, including a crowned woman before an enthroned ruler, the wheels of her torture shattered by an angel, and her body laid in a tomb on a mountain. On the right, the story of Saint Blaise, a bishop in red, including his life in a cave among animals, his torture at a post and his execution.
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Altar Dossal with the Crucifixion, the Mystic Pelican and Stories of Saints Catherine of Alexandria and Blaise, c. 1333. Tempera and gold on panel, 82 × 281 cm, Vatican City, Musei Vaticani (normally in the papal representative apartments). From the altar of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Probably commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto.
entry: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco

alt: Two gold-ground wooden panels one above the other, each divided into four rows. In each row two small relic recesses, framed in tooled gilt metal and lined with red fabric behind glass, alternate with two half-length haloed saints standing above red name bands in gold Gothic letters. Upper panel: James and Philip; Mark and Andrew; Peter, with keys, and Paul, with sword and book; Simon and Bartholomew. Lower panel: the Virgin in a white veil holding the Christ Child, and Saint Francis in a brown habit with a red cross and book; the bishop Saint Nicholas blessing, and the deacon Saint Stephen with palm and book; the deacon Saint Lawrence, and the bishop Saint Blaise with crozier; the bishop Saint Apollinaris with crozier, and the deacon Saint Vincent with palm. The haloes are decorated with punched dots and stars, and the gold surface shows fine cracking
caption: Maestro di Cesi (= Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco?), Reliquary Panel with Saints James, Philip, Mark, Andrew, Peter, Paul, Simon and Bartholomew; below: Reliquary Panel with the Virgin and Child and Saints Francis, Nicholas, Stephen, Lawrence, Blaise, Apollinaris and Vincent, late 1320s. Tempera and gold on panel, with glazed relic recesses lined in red fabric, 32 × 21 × 3 cm (each). Rome, Museo Nazionale di Palazzo Venezia (VIVE), inv. 10207-10208.
entry: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco

alt: Tall gabled panel on a gold ground in a gilt frame. Five roundels crown the gable: Christ blessing with a book at the centre and four Evangelists with books, some with animal heads. Below, the Crucifixion: angels catch Christ's blood in cups; on the left the Virgin swoons among the holy women; a tonsured friar kneels and kisses the foot of the cross; Saint John in pink stands beside it, and a haloed nun in black kneels in prayer; on the right, helmeted soldiers with spears and a red banner inscribed SPQR. Red bands divide four smaller scenes beneath: the Betrayal and the Flagellation, then the Last Supper and the Agony in the Garden
caption: Attributed to the Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco by Longhi (1973); the Vatican curators give the San Francesco polyptych to the Maestro di Fossa (see text). Crucifixion with Christ Blessing, the Four Evangelists and Scenes from the Passion, c. 1330 (?). Tempera and gold on gabled panel with roundels, 76 × 34.2 cm, Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana (storage). Recorded in 1771 in San Francesco, Montefalco (Perugia), on the altar of the Holy Name of Jesus.

alt: Panel painting on a gold ground in a moulded frame with a shaped top. Christ hangs on a tall black cross under a red titulus, blood running from his hands, side and feet down the cross onto the rock below. Two thieves hang on lower crosses at either side, their arms tied over the crossbars, and two grieving angels fly beside Christ. At the foot of the cross Saint Francis kneels and kisses Christ's bleeding feet. On the left the Virgin sinks to the ground in the arms of another holy woman, with other haloed mourners and soldiers with spears behind. On the right Saint John sits weeping on the ground; behind him stand a dark-skinned man holding the sponge on a reed, soldiers under a red banner, one in a red dotted tunic pointing upward, and a group of elders.
caption: Maestro di Cesi (= Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco?), Crucifixion with the Two Thieves, the Holy Women, Saint John and Saint Francis, c. 1330 (?). Tempera and gold on panel, 66 × 79.5 cm. Bordighera, Collezione Terruzzi.

alt: Left wing of a small painted reliquary diptych with a worn, raised wooden frame. Above, on a darkened gold ground, the Virgin in a white veil and dark green mantle sits on a block throne holding the Christ Child in pink, between two bishop saints: Blaise in red and Nicholas in green. A red band below names them in white letters. In the middle a glazed recess holds relics wrapped in small paper labels written in ink. Below stand five saints over a red inscribed band: Bartholomew with a knife, Mary Magdalene covered in her long hair, the bishop Urban, Agatha in a white veil, and Anthony Abbot in a brown habit with a red book; Right wing of a small painted reliquary diptych with a worn, raised wooden frame. Above, on a darkened gold ground, Christ hangs on the cross with blood running from his wounds; a tiny kneeling monk in a black habit embraces the foot of the cross. Beside the cross stand the Virgin in black and Saint John in pink looking up, flanked by two female saints in white and pale blue-grey robes. A red band names them in white letters. In the middle a glazed recess holds bone fragments and folded paper relic labels. Below stand a bishop saint in a golden chasuble with crozier and two female saints in maroon and green, over a red band naming Saint Emilian and Saint Constantia
caption: Workshop of the Maestro di Sant'Alò according to the museum, not the Primo Maestro and shown for comparison: The Virgin and Child with Saints Blasius and Nicholas, Saints Bartholomew, Mary Magdalen, Urban, Agatha and Anthony (Left wing of a reliquary diptych); The Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint John, Saints Scholastica and Agnes and a Monastic Donor; Saints Emilian, Constantia (?) and an Unidentified Female Saint (Right wing of a reliquary diptych), c. 1320. Tempera and gold on panel, with a glazed relic compartment; width of the open diptych 32.8 cm. London, Victoria and Albert Museum, inv. 19-1869, 20-1869.
entry: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco

alt: Shaped wooden cross painted on a gold ground, with a black inner band running along the arms and the upright. At the top, a red titulus. Christ hangs dead with outstretched arms, head bowed under a crown of thorns and a gilded halo. His pale body is marked by small red wounds, and a jet of blood spurts from his side in a wide arc. He wears a translucent white loincloth with brown stripes. His feet are crossed and fixed with a single nail, blood flowing from the wound, and a small skull lies at the foot of the cross
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Painted Cross with the Crucified Christ, first half of the 14th century. Tempera and gold on shaped panel. Spoleto, church of San Domenico.
