The chapel's ceiling: a barrel of deep ultramarine sown with ranks of gold eight-pointed stars, divided into two fields; this one carries the Madonna and Child at the centre, attended by four prophets — the painted heaven under which the entire cycle unfolds.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Bust of Christ on a gold ground within a circular border of overlapping feather-like strokes shading from orange-gold to white. He wears a red tunic with an embroidered gold neckband and a blue mantle over his left shoulder; his right hand is raised in blessing with two extended fingers, his left supports a grey-green book with bossed studs and a central stamped rosette. His halo is radiate gold with a dark inscribed cross. Four gold eight-pointed stars occupy the blue corners outside the ring; an old vertical crack runs through the tondo.
caption: The Blessing Redeemer, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. The central clipeus of one of the vault's two fields: Christ half-length on gold within a feathered rainbow ring, a cross inscribed in his radiate halo, blessing with the right hand and holding a studded, rosette-stamped book in the left, among eight-pointed stars.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length figure of an old man on a gold ground within a feathered ring shading red to white with green inner edge. He has a long white beard and balding white hair, a radiate gold halo, and wears an orange-red mantle over a blue tunic whose collar carries a band of pseudo-script embroidery. Both hands hold an unrolled scroll inscribed with lines of illegible pseudo-writing; his head turns in three-quarter view, eyes raised to his right.
caption: A Prophet, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. One of the eight prophet-clipei attending the central tondi: a white-bearded seer in an orange mantle over blue, holding an unrolled scroll of pseudo-script, his gaze lifted across the stars toward the centre of his field.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length figure of an old man on a gold ground within a feathered white-and-pink ring. He is seen in near profile facing left, with long grey-white hair falling to his shoulders and a full white beard; a worn radiate halo surrounds his head. He wears a red mantle clasped at the chest over a dark tunic; his right hand is raised open beside his face, his left rests at his breast.
caption: A Prophet, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. One of the eight prophet-clipei: an aged seer wrapped in a red mantle, in near profile, the right hand lifted open in the orator's gesture — prophecy as speech, turned toward the centre of the starry field.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length figure of a man on a bright gold ground within a feathered ring of deep red shading to white. He has short greying hair, a high forehead and a trimmed grey beard, with a worn radiate halo. He wears a violet-red mantle over a blue-grey tunic, its edges and central band richly bordered in gold embroidery; both hands are raised open at chest height, and his head turns in three-quarter view, eyes lifted to his right.
caption: A Prophet, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. One of the eight prophet-clipei: a seer in a violet-red mantle hemmed with broad gold embroidery, both hands raised toward the centre of the field — prophecy as adoration, the seer become witness.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length figure of a man on a gold ground within a feathered ring of dusky rose shading to white with a blue-green inner edge. He has long dark hair falling past his shoulders, a dark beard and moustache, and a radiate halo worn to traces on the gold, which is spotted with small losses. He wears a shaggy camel-hair tunic under a rose mantle with a gold-bordered hem; his right hand is raised in blessing, his left gathers the edge of his mantle.
caption: St John the Baptist, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. The one nameable figure among the vault's eight satellite clipei: the Forerunner in his camel-hair tunic under a rose mantle, blessing with one hand and gathering his mantle with the other — the hinge between the prophets' heaven and the Gospel unfolding on the walls below.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length frontal figure of the Virgin on a gold ground, wearing a rose veil over a dark blue mantle, her radiate gold halo behind the veil. She holds the Child on her left arm, her right hand laid across her body toward him; the Child, in a pale gold-hemmed tunic with a radiate halo, sits frontally, one hand at his breast. The ring is a broad gold band ornamented with lines of pseudo-script, crossed by paired chevron fillets and set with four quadrilobe medallions at the cardinal points. Gold eight-pointed stars surround the tondo in the blue.
caption: The Madonna and Child, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. The central clipeus of the vault's second field: the Virgin frontal with the Child on her arm, both gazing straight down, within a broad gold ring banded with pseudo-script and quadrilobe medallions — the chapel's dedicatee enthroned in its sky, ringed by the four prophets of the Incarnation.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length figure of an old bald-crowned man on a gold ground, within a ring of red bands bearing pseudo-script, white chevron fillets and quadrilobe rosettes. He has a long forked white beard and a radiate gold halo, and wears a rose mantle clasped over a crimson tunic with an embroidered collar. His right hand is raised open beside his face; his left holds a long white scroll that passes behind his shoulder and falls, unbroken, out of the tondo’s frame, inscribed in Gothic letters with the opening of Isaiah 7:14.
caption: The Prophet Isaiah, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. One of the four prophets attending the Madonna's clipeus, identified by his scroll: Ecce virgo concipiet et pariet filium… (Isaiah 7:14) — the Annunciation's own prophecy, in the chapel consecrated on the Annunciation's feast.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length figure of an old man on a gold ground, within a ring of red pseudo-script bands, white chevron fillets and quadrilobe rosettes. White hair frames his head like a cloth, over a full grey-white beard; his radiate halo is worn. He wears a salmon-pink mantle with gold-embroidered borders over a red tunic, and points a finger at his chest with his right hand while his left grasps a white scroll that unrolls out of the tondo, inscribed in Gothic letters.
caption: The Prophet Baruch, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. One of the four prophets of the Madonna's field, identified by his scroll: Hic est Deus noster… (Baruch 3:36) — the verse whose continuation, "afterward he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men," made Baruch a prophet of the Incarnation.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length figure of an old man on a gold ground, within a ring of red pseudo-script bands, white chevron fillets and quadrilobe rosettes. He is balding with short grey hair and a grey-white beard, his radiate halo on worn gold; he wears a blue mantle over a green tunic with a gold-embroidered collar. His right hand is raised before his chest, the forefinger pointing upward; his left holds a white scroll that unrolls downward out of the tondo, inscribed in Gothic letters.
caption: The Prophet Malachi, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. One of the four prophets of the Madonna's field, identified by his scroll: Et statim veniet… (Malachi 3:1) — "the Lord whom you seek shall suddenly come to his temple," the prophecy of the Presentation painted twice on the walls below.

alt: Fresco tondo by Giotto in the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Half-length figure of a beardless young man on a gold ground, within a ring of red pseudo-script bands, white chevron fillets and quadrilobe rosettes. He has dark hair curling to the jaw, a radiate halo on darkened gold, a gold collar at his neck, and wears a pale blue mantle over a dark gold-patterned tunic. His right hand is raised with pointing finger; his left holds a long white scroll that unrolls downward out of the tondo, headed DANIEL and inscribed with further Gothic lines.
caption: The Prophet Daniel, vault tondo, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. One of the four prophets of the Madonna's field — and the only figure in the vault who bears his own name, written at the head of his scroll: DANIEL, above the words of Daniel 6:26 on the living God whose kingdom shall not be destroyed.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Within a quatrefoil frame set in a square panel of fictive Cosmatesque mosaic — red-and-white triangular tesserae at the corners, pale foliage sprays in the spandrels — a balding elder with grey hair and beard, wrapped in a mauve-pink mantle, bends his head over a naked infant lying across his arms. His right hand is lowered toward the child’s body, the blade itself not shown; the infant reaches one arm up toward the old man’s face, without touching it. Bands of fictive marble inlay flank the panel; fragments of adjacent quadrilobe panels appear above and below.
caption: The Circumcision, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. One of the small quatrefoil scenes set into the painted ornamental bands that frame the narrative cycle: a bearded elder bends over a naked infant held against his side, the blade scarcely visible, while the child reaches up toward his face — the rite of the eighth day, compressed to two figures and one act.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a full vertical strip of fictive ornament. At the centre, a quatrefoil opens onto a scene: a tawny lion, ribs showing, stands in profile and lowers his maned head, mouth open, over a group of small cubs lying on pale rocky ground — one stretched flat, the others lifting their muzzles toward him — against a blue sky with a tree now darkened to near-black. Above and below the quatrefoil run interlaced bands of fictive Cosmatesque inlay with triangular mosaic panels, and lozenge fields of red, white and blue acanthus scrollwork close the strip at top and bottom.
caption: The Lion Reviving His Cubs, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, lower register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Lamentation and the Noli me tangere: the lion of the bestiaries bends over his cubs, born dead, to wake them on the third day with his breath — the figure of the Resurrection, stationed at the exact seam where the cycle leaves the Resurrection itself unpainted.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a full vertical strip of fictive ornament. At the centre, a quatrefoil opens onto a scene: an elderly bald-crowned man with a white beard, wrapped in an ochre-yellow mantle, stands in profile facing right and extends a slender rod toward a mass of pale rock filling the right lobe. Above and below, dark porphyry-like panels framed in white hold symmetrical acanthus candelabra, each sprouting around a small human face amid the foliage; a pilaster strip of Cosmatesque lozenge mosaic runs up the right edge.
caption: Moses Brings Forth Water out of the Rock, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, middle register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Baptism of Christ and the Marriage at Cana: Moses alone, rod in hand, touches the desert rock with his rod — the water-miracle of the old covenant stationed between the two water-miracles of the new, under Paul’s own gloss: “and the rock was Christ.”

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a full vertical strip of fictive ornament. At the centre, a quatrefoil opens onto a sea: stylised grey-green waves fill the lower lobes, and from them the pale body of a great fish rears up out of the water in the act of swallowing a man head-first — only his bare legs still kick upward out of its gullet against the dark sky. Above and below the quatrefoil, dark porphyry-like panels framed in white hold symmetrical acanthus rosettes; a pilaster strip of Cosmatesque mosaic runs up the right edge.
caption: Jonah Swallowed up by the Whale, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, lower register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Crucifixion and the Lamentation, directly below the Moses of the rock: only the prophet’s legs remain above the waves as the great fish takes him head-first — the sign of Jonah, the one type Christ claimed for himself, posted at the threshold of the three days.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a full vertical strip of fictive ornament. At the centre, a quatrefoil opens onto a scene: at the left, the Creator — a bearded figure with Christ’s features, a gold radiate halo inscribed with a cross, a red garment under a blue mantle now somewhat darkened — bends forward with both hands extended; at the right, a naked beardless young man, Adam, half-rises from the pale ground, one arm reaching up toward the Creator’s hands. Above and below the quatrefoil, dark porphyry-like panels framed in white hold symmetrical acanthus candelabra sprouting around small foliate faces; a pilaster strip of Cosmatesque mosaic runs up the right edge.
caption: The Creation of Adam, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, middle register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Marriage at Cana and the Raising of Lazarus: the Creator, bearing the face and halo of Christ, bends over the naked Adam rising from the ground — the first creation stationed beside the second, where Lazarus is called back from the earth Adam was made of.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a full vertical strip of fictive ornament. At the centre, a quatrefoil opens onto a scene: at the left, an old man with long white hair and a long white beard, wrapped in a rose-red mantle, bends in profile toward the right; immediately before him, in a darkened zone, a hand grasps the red mantle; beyond, filling the right lobes, four bare-headed youths press close, their faces upturned in a row. Neither elder bears a halo. Above and below the quatrefoil, dark panels framed in white hold symmetrical acanthus candelabra sprouting around small foliate faces; a pilaster strip of Cosmatesque mosaic runs up the right edge.
caption: The Prophet Elisha and the Youths (Elijah and Elisha with the Sons of the Prophets), quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, middle register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Raising of Lazarus and the Entry into Jerusalem: an old prophet bends toward four youths while a second elder grasps his red mantle — the last journey of 2 Kings 2, the disciple who will not let go and the prophetic school in attendance, stationed directly above the fiery chariot that will take the master up.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a full vertical strip of fictive ornament. At the centre, a quatrefoil opens onto a blue sky: a white-robed, white-haired prophet with a darkened halo stands in a two-wheeled cart, his left arm raised; cart, wheels and the single galloping horse that draws it upward to the right are all painted the same flame-red, with plumes of fire about them; no reins are shown. In his right hand he still holds his pale mantle, which streams away toward the lower left lobe — where the face and reaching right arm of a young man stretch up toward it from the margin's edge. Above and below the quatrefoil run interlaced bands of fictive Cosmatesque inlay, and lozenge fields of red acanthus scrollwork close the strip at top and bottom.
caption: Elijah on the Chariot of Fire, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, lower register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Noli me tangere and the Ascension, directly below Elisha holding the master's hem: the prophet rides upward in a two-wheeled cart drawn by a horse of flame, his left arm raised in farewell, the pale mantle still in his right hand and streaming toward a young Elisha who reaches up for it from the lower lobe — the old covenant's rapture stationed beside the new covenant's ascension.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a full vertical strip of fictive ornament. At the centre, a quatrefoil opens onto a blue sky with pale clouds: from the upper right a bearded figure with Christ’s features bends down, his darkened halo bearing traces of an inscribed cross, and delivers a single white tablet, unmarked by any writing; at the lower left an elderly bald-crowned man with a long white beard and a darkened halo of his own, wrapped in an ochre-yellow mantle, grasps the tablet with both hands. At the right, beside him, rises the bare rock of the mountain, which he does not touch. Above and below the quatrefoil run interlaced bands of fictive Cosmatesque inlay, and lozenge fields of red acanthus scrollwork close the strip at top and bottom.
caption: Moses on Mount Sinai, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, lower register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Ascension and the Pentecost: God, bearing Christ’s features, bends down from the sky to deliver the white tablet of the Law into the grasping hands of Moses — the Sinai of the fiftieth day stationed beside the Pentecost of the fiftieth day, the Law in stone beside the Law in fire.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip with two barbed quatrefoils on blue grounds, separated by a large panel of fictive rose marble in dark frames. In the upper quatrefoil, a young evangelist with short dark hair, a darkened halo, a pale tunic with an embroidered collar and a red mantle over one shoulder sits behind a wooden writing-desk, his right hand raised beside his face holding a slender pen, another pen lying on the desk. In the lower quatrefoil, an old evangelist with long white hair and beard and a darkened halo bends low over his wooden desk, reading his page, a darkened pen held still in his left hand.
caption: Two Evangelists, quadrilobes on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, lower register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the terminal band at the right of the Pentecost, where the cycle ends against the west wall: two haloed evangelists at their writing-desks — a young one pausing, pen raised, an old one bent close over his page — the story the walls have just told, caught in the act of becoming Scripture.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted ornamental band crossing the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip on deep red ground. At the top, a barbed quatrefoil on blue holds the bust of an old man with long flowing white hair and beard, a radiate gold halo and a red mantle, holding upright a darkened object that widens fan-wise as it rises past his left shoulder, perhaps a scourge, lower right, appears the small head and part of the bust of a child, his face turned up toward the elder. At the centre, blue acanthus scrollwork with gold flowers opens around the bust of a wingèd figure: a youthful face under a pointed leaf-like hood, grey-blue wings spread, a gold mantle clasped at the throat. At the bottom, a second barbed quatrefoil on blue holds the bust of a bearded man with a radiate gold halo and brown mantle, his right hand raised. Cosmatesque mosaic chevrons separate the compartments.
caption: Busts on the first decorative band of the vault (detail), c. 1303–1305. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. A stretch of the first of the three ornamental arches that cross the starry vault, at the right of which opens the field of the blessing Redeemer: haloed busts of the old covenant’s holy ones in barbed quatrefoils on blue — an elder with a child at his shoulder among them — alternating with winged figures born out of the acanthus scrollwork.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted decorative band on the north wall of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip. At top and bottom, barbed quatrefoils on grey-blue grounds each hold the bust of an elderly bearded man with a radiate gold halo and a rose-red mantle over a pale tunic. The upper elder, short grey-bearded, lays his right hand flat against his breast; the lower, long-bearded, rests his left hand on a staff. The blue of the grounds survives patchily, the azurite fallen in places.
caption: Decorative band with busts, detail, c. 1303–1305. Fresco. North wall, upper register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. From the painted band at the left of the Birth of the Virgin: two haloed elders in barbed quatrefoils, one hand laid to the breast and the other on a staff, separated by a panel of fictive marble and flanked by candelabra strips — the crowned ancestors of the margins, stationed at the threshold of the birth their whole order waited for.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted decorative band in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip of fictive grey-green veined marble, bordered by ochre candelabra strips. At the centre, a barbed quatrefoil on a blue-grey ground holds the bust of a beardless young man with short dark hair and a radiate gold halo, wearing a pale mantle over a tunic, his right hand laid flat on the breast, his left holding a small closed red book, plain and unclasped, against his chest. Above and below the quatrefoil, two white lozenge frames enclose red cross-shaped leaf ornaments, with small gemmed squares at their points.
caption: Bust of a young saint with a book, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between Joachim Expelled from the Temple and Joachim among the Shepherds (placement uncertain), south wall, upper register: a beardless young saint with a radiate halo, a red book held against the breast, in a barbed quatrefoil set in fictive grey-veined marble between two gemmed lozenge-crosses — a reader of the new covenant among the margins' crowned company.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted decorative band in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip that narrows slightly toward the top. In the upper barbed quatrefoil, on a dark ground, the bust of a beardless young saint with a radiate gold halo, in a pale mantle over red, his right index finger pointing across his own chest, his left hand holding a darkened upright object. In the lower quatrefoil, on a grey-blue ground, the bust of an old man with a radiate gold halo, unruly white hair and a long forked beard, his right hand raised before him, his left arm drawn across the body. Between them stands a tall plain cream-coloured panel in a painted frame; strips of candelabra ornament on ochre and brown flank the compartments.
caption: Decorative band with busts, detail, c. 1303–1305. Fresco. Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. From the chapel’s painted framing system: two haloed busts in barbed quatrefoils — above, a young saint pointing across his chest with his right hand, a darkened object in his left; below, a wild-bearded elder with his right hand raised — separated by a tall pale panel and flanked by candelabra strips.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted decorative band in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip of fictive grey-green veined marble flecked with dark markings. At the centre, a barbed quatrefoil on a muted violet-grey ground holds the bust of a young man with shoulder-length light brown hair, a short beard, and a radiate gold halo, wearing a rose mantle over one shoulder and a pale garment on the other, his right hand drawn before his breast. Above and below, two white lozenge frames enclose red-and-gold cross-shaped leaf ornaments with small gemmed squares at their points.
caption: Bust of a young saint, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, c. 1303–1305. Fresco. North wall, upper register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Marriage of the Virgin and the Wedding Procession: a long-haired young saint with a radiate halo, his right hand drawn to his breast, in a barbed quatrefoil set in fictive grey-green marble between two gemmed lozenge-crosses — a witness of the margins posted between the vow and the procession.

alt: Polyptych of five panels on a gold ground, each under its own pointed gable. At the centre Christ, bearded and cross-haloed, in a red tunic and a green-grey mantle, raises his right hand in blessing and holds a red studded book. At the left stand a beardless young Saint John the Evangelist in pink and green, holding a green book, and the Virgin in a grey veil and dark blue mantle, her hand laid on her breast. At the right stand Saint John the Baptist, bearded, in a red mantle, a scroll in his hand, and Saint Francis in a brown habit, his hands crossed on his chest.
caption: The Peruzzi Altarpiece, c. 1310–1315, tempera and gilded gesso on poplar, five panels, just over 1 m high and 2.5 m wide. Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation, 1961. The probable altarpiece of the Peruzzi Chapel: Christ blessing between Saint John the Evangelist, the Virgin, Saint John the Baptist and Saint Francis.

alt: Heavily stained and darkened vellum page from the Book of Mulling, with a single narrow column of small Irish minuscule script on the left containing the end of John's Gospel and the opening of the colophon; further colophon lines naming the scribe Mulling survive at the upper right, and long diagonal tears across the blank right half of the leaf are closed with stitched vellum repairs.
caption: Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 60 (Book of Mulling), folio 94r. The recto of the manuscript's last leaf carries the closing portion of the Gospel of John — a later annotation at the foot of the column reads "Joh. 21."

alt: Severely stained brown vellum leaf, the last of the Book of Mulling. Faint lines of small Irish minuscule containing a liturgical office survive in the upper left; the circular diagram — two barely visible concentric circles with faded Irish captions — occupies the lower centre of the page. A long branching tear runs diagonally across the middle of the leaf, closed with visible zigzag thread stitching, and a large irregular lighter repair patch fills the damaged upper right corner.
caption: Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 60 (Book of Mulling), folio 94v. The verso of the last leaf carries, side by side, a compressed devotional office and the manuscript's most debated image: two concentric circles, only a few centimetres across, ringed and filled with captioned crosses, with the four cardinal points written in Irish. On Lawlor's reading the outer line of writing names the crosses of Mark at the south, Matthew at the west, John at the north and Luke at the east, and the inner line names the prophets Jeremiah, Daniel and Ezekiel, with a fourth, Isaiah, restored; four further crosses inside the circles bear partly effaced captions naming the Holy Spirit, gifts, angels from above, and Christ with his apostles.

alt: Full-page miniature from the Book of Mulling showing a haloed, frontal standing evangelist with orange hair, wearing a mauve cloak over a blue tunic, its folds drawn as interlaced gold-edged bands; he holds a book against his chest with one hand laid flat over it. The figure stands in a rectangular frame with knotwork squares at the corners and tall side panels of interlaced elongated animal ornament on blue grounds; his halo overlaps the top of the frame. The vellum leaf is browned and worn at the edges
caption: Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 60 (Book of Mulling), folio 81v. The portrait of John, the only evangelist portrait illustrated here; the identification rests on position alone, for the figure carries no inscription and no evangelist symbol. The number 53 at the upper right is the older numbering of the British Museum binders.

alt: Front face of the medieval book-shrine of the Book of Mulling: a rectangular metal box with worn silver surface, dominated by a large polished oval rock crystal held by dark claw mounts at the centre; rows of gilt Gothic lettering on silver foil are visible magnified through the crystal. Around it are several smaller settings — dark red and brown oval polished stones in decorated mounts, a small cross-shaped fitting and plain bosses — framed by twisted rope-like mouldings, with dents and losses at the corners. The shrine stands on a pale surface in a museum display
caption: Shrine (cumdach) of the Book of Mulling, from St Mullins, Co. Carlow; principal phase c. 1402, with settings added at various later dates. The box is built of copper-alloy sheets partly covered with silver and, unlike the shrine of the Book of Dimma, is ornamented on its front face only, which carries a deliberately heterogeneous display of eight settings accumulated over the object's history — polished oval cabochons in collared mounts, a small cross-shaped setting, and plain bosses, framed by rope-twist mouldings.

alt: Illuminated manuscript page on purple ground framed by gold foliate interlace: a tonsured archbishop in orange-red vestments sits enthroned holding a long staff, flanked by two small monks in blue-grey habits offering golden books; gold inscriptions name Egbertus, Keraldus and Heribertus

The square halo marks Egbert as a living dignitary. Trier, Stadtbibliothek, Hs. 24, c. 980s.

alt: Large medieval fresco of the Triumph of Death by Buonamico Buffalmacco in the Camposanto of Pisa, c. 1336–41. At left, richly dressed riders halt before three coffins holding decaying corpses while a hermit displays a scroll; above, anchorites live peacefully in a rocky wilderness. At centre, Death as a winged hag with a scythe swoops over a mound of dead popes, kings, and nobles, as angels and demons fight over small nude souls. At right, young men and women make music in an orange grove, unaware of Death approaching.
caption: The Triumph of Death, 1336-41, fresco, 560 x 1500 cm, Camposanto Monumentale (South Wall), Pisa.
entry: The Baptistery of San Giovanni and the Camposanto Monumentale, Pisa

alt: Medieval fresco of Hell by Buonamico Buffalmacco in the Camposanto of Pisa, c. 1336–41. Hell is shown as the interior of a rocky mountain divided into levels where devils torment naked sinners with serpents, fire, a boiling cauldron, and a dragon's maw. At the centre a gigantic horned, tusked Lucifer chews one sinner while another emerges from a second face at his belly. At the left, haloed apostles and angels with the Cross preside as crowned and mitred figures among the damned are driven toward the abyss. Painted scrolls with inscriptions label the sins and punishments.
caption: Hell, 1336-41, fresco, Camposanto Monumentale (South Wall), Pisa.
entry: The Baptistery of San Giovanni and the Camposanto Monumentale, Pisa

alt: Large medieval fresco of the Thebaid by Buonamico Buffalmacco in the Camposanto of Pisa, c. 1336–41, showing the desert of the Egyptian hermits as a rocky landscape with palms and small chapels. Dozens of episodes from the lives of the Desert Fathers appear across the mountain: Mary of Egypt, covered by her own hair, kneels before the monk Zosimas; lions recall the legend of Paul the Hermit; a hermit at upper right confronts a winged demon; other monks weave baskets, dig, read, and pray. Along the bottom the Nile, full of fish, separates the desert from a walled city, with a camel driver, a fisherman, and a rider crossing a bridge.
